rows.title: IconChevronDown (disclosure chevron)
rows.detail: ChevronDownIcon exists — same Fluent slug (chevron_down_20_regular), exact match. Icon-sizing rule (see A-6 for the same explanation): bidezine sources every icon from Fluent's 20px-regular grid (100% of icons/manifest.json uses the _20_regular slug — that's fixed), but the ON-SCREEN render size is controlled per component via Tailwind size-* classes (e.g. buttons default unstyled icons to size-4/16px), not a fixed 20px display rule. So origin's size={16} in a 20px slot isn't a divergence — it's the same sourcing grid, just a smaller render size, which our components already support. User explicitly concurred with this reading and marked it decided — no further action needed.

rows.title: Panel header title/subtitle overflow behavior — not previously itemized
rows.detail: Prompted by “the title should truncate in a single line if the text is too large... i don't have a way to see this behaviour” — the demo content (“Slides”, “Documents”, etc.) is always short, so neither behavior was ever visually exercised before. TITLE: verified against design-system/src/gallery/RailNav.tsx's real, current source — origin renders the title with `whiteSpace: nowrap; textOverflow: ellipsis` (single-line truncation). FunctionalRailSidebar.tsx's title span already used Tailwind's `truncate` (the exact equivalent) — confirmed working by temporarily substituting a long title and reading computed style (whiteSpace: nowrap, textOverflow: ellipsis, scrollWidth 674px clipped to a clientWidth of 202px). SUBTITLE: origin's real source WRAPS the subtitle unbounded (`whiteSpace: normal`, no line cap at all — a 2026-07-31 change away from its earlier single-line truncation, per the source's own code comment). rows.title: Panel actions / overflow menu row text renders at the shared primitive's text-sm default, not the already-approved text-xs (D-5/D-6)
rows.detail: Prompted by “is the font token consistent with our dropdown-menu?” Measured live via getComputedStyle: our rail's DropdownMenuItem/CheckboxItem rows (“Expand all”, “Collapse all”, “Search box”) render at 14px/400 Inter — exactly Tailwind's `text-sm`, hard-coded in dropdown-menu.tsx's own className for every item/checkbox/radio/sub-trigger row. Checked origin's real token source (design-system/src/tokens.ts): the equivalent origin rows use TYPE.bodyS (13px/400, unchecked) and TYPE.labelM (13px/500, checked) — and D-5/D-6 ALREADY approved a bidezine mapping for exactly those two origin tokens: text-xs for “compact secondary/menu text” (D-5) and text-xs font-medium for “checked rows” (D-6). So the actually-rendered menu text (text-sm/14px) diverges from D-5/D-6's mapping for this exact origin content. Root cause is structural, not a copy mistake: origin's PanelMenuRow is fully custom-styled (Radix is unstyled; origin applies TYPE.bodyS/labelM via inline `style` on every row itself), while our dropdown-menu.tsx is the shadcn-styled wrapper, where text-sm is shadcn's own deliberate, SHARED, system-wide default across every menu-family primitive (Menubar, Select, Context Menu, Command all use it too) — not something scoped to the rail. DECIDED: keep text-sm, do not override — the shared bidezine dropdown-menu convention takes precedence over matching this one origin instance's smaller scale. This was floated as a live code change (className overrides + a screenshot) to see it rendered, then explicitly reverted at the user's instruction (“i didn't want you to change anything, i only asked, the recommendation to leave it as it is was right”) — no diff was ever committed. D-5/D-6 remain correctly approved for the other bidezine surfaces that actually use bare text-xs directly (not this shared Radix-menu primitive); this row documents that the dropdown-menu family is treated as a separate, deliberately-consistent scale, not a D-5/D-6 violation. For contrast: the rail's OTHER dropdown (overflow “More” menu) was checked too and needs no such call — origin's own overflow menu already uses TYPE.bodyM/labelL (14px), which maps cleanly to our already-approved text-sm/text-sm font-medium (D-4/D-7), so there was never a real conflict there.

rows.title: The rail must fill its container's full available height, not size itself intrinsically
rows.detail: APPROVED. DEPLOYMENT NOTE, not a divergence: FunctionalRailSidebar's outer wrapper takes an explicit `height` NUMBER prop and applies it via inline style — in this limbo-factory preview that number comes from App.tsx's FillHeight, which measures its parent stage's clientHeight with a ResizeObserver and passes it down (see LAYOUT.md). That measurement plumbing is preview-tool-specific, NOT something to carry over verbatim into the real src/ui/ component. At real Build time, the shipped component should instead rely on ordinary CSS sizing (e.g. `h-full` on its outer element, assuming the consumer's own layout gives it a definite height via something like `h-screen` further up the tree) rather than requiring a measured-height prop — the underlying requirement is simply “the rail fills whatever vertical space its parent gives it,” not “the rail must be told its height in pixels.” User explicitly approved this guidance (see divergence row L-47) — no code change needed in limbo-factory itself (the measured-height prop is deliberately correct FOR THIS PREVIEW TOOL, not a bug to fix here), but this note is now locked in as an explicit, signed-off Build-time requirement rather than a left-as-guidance suggestion, so a future Build implementation does not silently carry the preview's ResizeObserver-measured-height plumbing into the shipped component.

rows.title: The footer group (Profile + Settings) visually anchors to the bottom of the rail
rows.detail: APPROVED. DEPLOYMENT NOTE, now confirmed live in code: the footer's bottom position is NOT achieved by reversing DOM order or absolute/fixed positioning — the rail is a single flex column (logo → divider → nav → divider → footer) where the middle nav section alone carries `flex min-h-0 flex-1 flex-col gap-1` (verified live at the real `trackRef` div, FunctionalRailSidebar.tsx), so it grows to consume all left-over vertical space and pushes everything after it (the second divider + footer group) down to the bottom edge. Within the footer group itself, items still render in normal top-to-bottom reading order (Profile above Settings) — only the GROUP as a whole is bottom-anchored, not each item individually reversed. Any real Build-time reimplementation must preserve this same flex-1-spacer mechanism (not a manual top/bottom split or absolute positioning) so the footer continues to sit flush at the bottom regardless of how many pinned sections are above it. No code change needed; documentation-only sign-off.

rows.title: SCROLL.css / SCROLL.className (custom scrollbar styling)
rows.detail: Prompted by “if you already did the audit why are we using that scrollbar if we have our native scrollbar from our system?” This was already a tracked, open decision (three options: our ScrollArea component, browser-default, or a custom stylesheet) that the previous “exhaustive” audit pass didn't happen to check (it covered className merges and interactive states, not which scrollbar mechanism was in use) — not a new bug, but a pre-existing gap the audit's own scope hadn't reached yet. Checked origin's real approach first: origin uses `SCROLL.css`/`SCROLL.className`, a runtime <style> tag injection — already ruled out elsewhere in this same tracker (R-7, K-1/K-2) as incompatible with this project's build-time Tailwind CSS approach, so it was never a valid target to match anyway. DECIDED (option a): swapped the panel content's plain `overflow-y-auto` div for the real ScrollArea/ScrollBar primitives (Radix-based, exported from @bidezine/system). Required a rebuild of the root package first — ScrollArea existed in src/ui/scroll-area.tsx and was exported from src/index.ts, but the built dist/index.js that limbo-factory's `file:..` dependency resolves against was stale and didn't include it yet; ran `npm run build` at the repo root to regenerate dist/, then cleared limbo-factory's Vite dependency cache to pick up the fresh build. FOLLOW-UP REGRESSION (“i am not able to scroll anymore”): the initial swap genuinely broke scrolling — confirmed via getComputedStyle that the new viewport's scrollHeight EQUALED its clientHeight (424px both), i.e. nothing overflowed at all. Root cause: unlike the plain `overflow-y-auto` div it replaced, ScrollArea's own Root recipe never sets its own `overflow` (stays at the CSS default, `visible`), and CSS flexbox's “automatic minimum size: 0” rule — the mechanism that let the OLD div correctly shrink to the parent's available height — only applies to flex items whose own overflow is non-`visible`. With `overflow: visible`, the Root just grew to fit its content's natural height instead of being clipped, so there was nothing left to scroll. Fixed by adding `overflow-hidden` explicitly to the ScrollArea's className, restoring that automatic-minimum-size behavior. Verified via getComputedStyle after the fix: viewport scrollHeight (424px) now correctly exceeds clientHeight (397px), and via live wheel-scroll interaction that scrollTop actually advances and the scrollbar thumb visibly appears (screenshot-confirmed in both light and dark app modes). SELF-CRITICAL NOTE: the original K-3 fix's “verified via live interaction” claim was not actually a correct verification — that check used `document.querySelector`, which returns only the FIRST matching element in DOM order, and the page's own outer “Human Decisions” content list also uses a real ScrollArea and happens to appear earlier in the DOM than the rail's panel tree — so that initial check was silently testing the wrong scroll area the whole time, the same “wrong element targeted” mistake made once already earlier in this same fix. The rail's own scrolling was never actually confirmed working before this regression was reported. Lesson folded into CLAUDE.md's Primitive Fidelity Checklist: when multiple instances of the same primitive can exist on a page, a verification query must be scoped/disambiguated explicitly (index, container, or a distinguishing selector) — `querySelector`/`.first()` defaulting to “whichever matches first” is not a safe verification target.

rows.title: LogoSlotDark
rows.detail: No direct bidezine primitive; composable from a plain button + our Tooltip. Behavior requirement (verified against design-system/src/gallery/LogoSlotDark.tsx, not re-derived from memory): the tooltip shows on hover UNCONDITIONALLY — even when the slot has no onClick/isInteractive — with the logo label (default "BiDezine", see M-9). REGRESSION FOUND AND FIXED this session: the L-51 color-contract refactor extracted the logo's inline `<a>`/`<div>` markup into a new `RailLogoSlot` component sitting directly under `<TooltipTrigger asChild>`, and this silently broke the tooltip in TWO separate, compounding ways, neither caught by typecheck/build. (1) `RailLogoSlot` was a plain function component, not `React.forwardRef` — Radix's `asChild`/Slot mechanism needs a ref forwarded to the real DOM node to attach hover tracking; a non-forwarding component silently swallows that ref with no error. (2) even after adding `forwardRef`, the component destructured only its own known props (`href`/`colors`/`children`) and dropped everything else — which silently discarded the additional props (`onPointerEnter`/`onPointerLeave`/`onFocus`/`onBlur`/`data-state`, etc.) Radix's Slot clones onto the child to actually detect hover/focus. Verified live via Playwright against the running limbo-factory dev server (both failure modes reproduced a real `null` tooltip query before either fix, confirmed passing after both): non-interactive logo (no logoHref, current default) now shows its tooltip ("BiDezine") unconditionally on hover; a temporarily-wired interactive logo (logoHref set) shows the tooltip AND correct hover/press color transitions simultaneously, with no regression to L-51's color contract (non-interactive logo still has zero hover/press color change, confirmed via getComputedStyle). Fix + full rationale documented directly in `RailLogoSlot`'s own doc comment in FunctionalRailSidebar.tsx so a future refactor doesn't reintroduce either failure mode silently.

rows.title: PanelTree leaf rows showed zero hover feedback (group rows worked); Button's real primitive has no built-in press/active state anywhere in the system
rows.detail: Prompted by “why only parents have states reaction on hover, and is our design system ignoring/omitting press state for this particular primitive... we don't want to reinvent the wheel, we want to use real and existing components, but we want to make sure they're implemented correctly and consistently.” TWO separate findings, verified via getComputedStyle before touching anything: (1) HOVER BUG (leaf rows only): the leaf Button's inline `style` unconditionally set `background: isSelected ? "var(--foreground)" : "transparent"` — an inline style value ALWAYS wins over a class-based rule for the same CSS property regardless of specificity or pseudo-state, so the literal "transparent" permanently blocked the button's own `hover:bg-accent` class from ever visually applying. Measured: unselected leaf hover stayed rgba(0,0,0,0) (no tint), while sibling group-toggle rows — which had NO competing inline background — correctly showed the accent tint on hover (oklch(0.97 0 0)), which is exactly why only parents appeared to react. This is the same failure-class as M-12 (a competing style silently blocking a real interactive class with no replacement wired in). FIXED by omitting the `background` property entirely when not selected (instead of setting it to the string "transparent"), letting the real `hover:bg-accent` class govern the resting/hover background as the primitive intends; a selected row still keeps its solid persistent highlight (verified: selected rows stay solid on hover too, matching conventional “active row doesn't need extra hover treatment” UX). Verified via getComputedStyle after the fix: unselected leaf hover now measures oklch(0.97 0 0), matching group rows, and by screenshot. (2) PRESS/ACTIVE STATE (system-wide, not rail-specific): checked bidezine's real Button primitive (src/ui/button.tsx) against the currently-vendored reference/shadcn-ui button.tsx — byte-identical for every variant (default/destructive/outline/secondary/ghost/link): NONE of them define an `active:`/press-state background class anywhere. This is confirmed NOT a bidezine omission — it faithfully matches the single, real, current upstream source; shadcn's own Button, as vendored today, ships zero built-in press-surface feedback for any variant. The only “active” wiring Button.tsx has (`useActionIconFill`'s `pressed`/`hovered`/`active` tracking) drives ONLY the inner Fluent icon's regular→filled swap (the approved Q1 rule) — it does not touch the button's own background/surface at all. So real press-state SURFACE feedback in this system is never automatic; it has to be deliberately wired per-instance with local hover/pressed state + real tokens, exactly the pattern already used for RailIconButton (M-12). IMPORTANT: the specific color a pressed PanelTree row (leaf or group) should use on this light panel surface is NOT yet an approved value — it's the exact same open, unresolved question as rows C-6 (hoverBg), C-7 (bgSubtle/checked), C-8 (activeBg/pressed), and C-9 (pressedOverlay), all still status: "decision" in the Color Token Lab. Left OPEN, not invented: adding manual press-state wiring to PanelTree rows requires C-6/C-8 to be resolved first so the pressed color is a real, approved token rather than an AI-invented one — the hover fix above only restores the primitive's OWN existing default (--accent, no new decision needed); press-state wiring is deferred pending C-6/C-8.

originRecord.detail: Prompted by “why only parents have states reaction on hover, and is our design system ignoring/omitting press state for this particular primitive... we don't want to reinvent the wheel, we want to use real and existing components, but we want to make sure they're implemented correctly and consistently.” TWO separate findings, verified via getComputedStyle before touching anything: (1) HOVER BUG (leaf rows only): the leaf Button's inline `style` unconditionally set `background: isSelected ? "var(--foreground)" : "transparent"` — an inline style value ALWAYS wins over a class-based rule for the same CSS property regardless of specificity or pseudo-state, so the literal "transparent" permanently blocked the button's own `hover:bg-accent` class from ever visually applying. Measured: unselected leaf hover stayed rgba(0,0,0,0) (no tint), while sibling group-toggle rows — which had NO competing inline background — correctly showed the accent tint on hover (oklch(0.97 0 0)), which is exactly why only parents appeared to react. This is the same failure-class as M-12 (a competing style silently blocking a real interactive class with no replacement wired in). FIXED by omitting the `background` property entirely when not selected (instead of setting it to the string "transparent"), letting the real `hover:bg-accent` class govern the resting/hover background as the primitive intends; a selected row still keeps its solid persistent highlight (verified: selected rows stay solid on hover too, matching conventional “active row doesn't need extra hover treatment” UX). Verified via getComputedStyle after the fix: unselected leaf hover now measures oklch(0.97 0 0), matching group rows, and by screenshot. (2) PRESS/ACTIVE STATE (system-wide, not rail-specific): checked bidezine's real Button primitive (src/ui/button.tsx) against the currently-vendored reference/shadcn-ui button.tsx — byte-identical for every variant (default/destructive/outline/secondary/ghost/link): NONE of them define an `active:`/press-state background class anywhere. This is confirmed NOT a bidezine omission — it faithfully matches the single, real, current upstream source; shadcn's own Button, as vendored today, ships zero built-in press-surface feedback for any variant. The only “active” wiring Button.tsx has (`useActionIconFill`'s `pressed`/`hovered`/`active` tracking) drives ONLY the inner Fluent icon's regular→filled swap (the approved Q1 rule) — it does not touch the button's own background/surface at all. So real press-state SURFACE feedback in this system is never automatic; it has to be deliberately wired per-instance with local hover/pressed state + real tokens, exactly the pattern already used for RailIconButton (M-12). IMPORTANT: the specific color a pressed PanelTree row (leaf or group) should use on this light panel surface is NOT yet an approved value — it's the exact same open, unresolved question as rows C-6 (hoverBg), C-7 (bgSubtle/checked), C-8 (activeBg/pressed), and C-9 (pressedOverlay), all still status: "decision" in the Color Token Lab. rows.title: PanelTree has no visual hierarchy guide line, unlike bidezine's own real Sidebar sub-menu (SidebarMenuSub) — RESOLVED, approved (see L-3)
rows.detail: Prompted by “something that brings to my attention is the sidebar example in our design system that has a leaf approach where a vertical line displays clearly the hierarchies, why didn't we use this approach?” Root cause of the earlier gap: L-9's investigation focused entirely on why the SidebarMenuButton/SidebarMenuSubButton COMPONENTS couldn't be reused (context-bound to a live <SidebarProvider>, depth-based size-shrinking convention, no real recursion support) — it only mentioned the vertical guide line in passing as “a nice touch” without separately evaluating it as its own, independently-adoptable piece. The line itself is NOT part of those button components at all — it's a plain `border-l` on SidebarMenuSub's own wrapper `<ul>` (`"mx-3.5 flex min-w-0 translate-x-px flex-col gap-1 border-l border-sidebar-border px-2.5 py-0.5"`), and none of L-9's three blockers actually apply to it: `--sidebar-border` is a real, globally-defined token in tokens.css (not scoped to a live Sidebar tree), and is currently IDENTICAL in value to bidezine's more general `--border` token in both light and dark mode (verified directly in tokens.css). PROPOSED and applied live for preview: added a `border-l` guide line (using the more general `--border` token, since this panel isn't a real Sidebar instance) to the wrapper around each recursed nesting level, replacing the old per-row `marginLeft: depth * 14` math (which would have double-counted the indent once a wrapper-level margin was introduced) with a compounding 16px-margin + 6px-padding step per recursion level — architecturally equivalent to how the real SidebarMenuSub's own indent naturally compounds through nested wrapping. Verified via screenshot in both light and dark app modes: a continuous vertical line now runs behind “Rules engine”/“Triggers”/“Schedules” (children of “System logic”), with a second, further-indented line for “Daily”/“Monthly”/“Yearly” (children of “Schedules”) — exactly the hierarchy cue requested, and it reads MORE clearly now that L-9 made every row the same size (the line becomes the primary depth cue instead of row size). APPROVED (user unavailable at decision time, explicitly instructed to proceed autonomously while reviewing L-3/L-4): compared directly against origin's real, more precise NavIndentLine.tsx atom (hairline/standard weight variants + negative-margin bleed-through-padding/gap continuity math) and decided the current simpler border-l approximation is sufficient — it already reads correctly and continuously in both themes, and the added complexity of exact bleed math isn't justified purely for line-continuity polish at this tree's actual density. See L-3 for the full comparison and the explicit note that this is a flagged simplification, not a silently-dropped requirement, should a denser future tree ever need the fuller technique.

rows.title: Guide line (L-11) didn't align under the parent's icon like the real Sidebar's does — traced to yet another has-[>svg]:px-3 vs px-2 conflict-group gap, the same recurring bug class as M-18/M-19
rows.detail: Prompted by “something is not right can you apply the same approach taken in the sidebar?” following L-11. Measured the real Sidebar's own guide line precisely (getBoundingClientRect on live localhost:4188/components/sidebar): its line sits almost exactly under the parent “Documentation” row's icon CENTER (1px off) — a deliberate design detail, not a coincidence. Measured our rail's equivalent: the line sat 6px to the LEFT of “System logic”'s icon center, because the icon itself was sitting 12px from the button's left edge instead of the intended 8px (`px-2`). Root cause: the leaf/group Button's default-size recipe carries `has-[>svg]:px-3` (a CONDITIONAL variant, 12px, active because these rows do contain an icon), and our own `px-2` override is a plain, unconditional utility — a DIFFERENT conflict group to tailwind-merge, so both survive and the base `has-[>svg]:px-3` kept winning the cascade (confirmed via twMerge directly: `twMerge('...has-[>svg]:px-3', '...px-2')` keeps both). This is the exact same recurring failure class as M-18 (Input's px-3 vs pl-7) and M-19 (Button's size-9 vs h-w) — the THIRD instance of it found this session, all traced to overriding a primitive's own conditional/shorthand utility with a plain or differently-scoped one. FIXED by repeating the override AS the same conditional variant (`has-[>svg]:px-2`, not just `px-2`), which IS in the same conflict group and correctly replaces the base rule — confirmed via twMerge directly. After the fix, also retuned the guide-line wrapper's margin (14px → 16px) to compensate for the now-correct 8px icon inset. Verified via getBoundingClientRect after both fixes: the guide line's x-position now matches the parent icon's center EXACTLY (0px difference) at both nesting levels (“System logic”→children and “Schedules”→children), matching the real Sidebar's own precision. Applied the same has-[>svg]:px-2 fix to both the leaf and group-toggle Button (they share the identical className); swept the rest of the file for the same pattern and found no other instances.

rows.title: Full box-model audit of PanelTree rows (height/radius/padding/gap/typography) — all aligned; one harmless underlying inconsistency found and normalized
rows.detail: Prompted by “is the height, rounded corners, padding and other aspects of these options aligned as well?” following the L-12 alignment fix. Measured every row type via getComputedStyle: leaf Button, group-toggle Button, the selected/active leaf, and the disabled leaf (a plain div, not a Button). Height (36px), border-radius (8px), horizontal padding (8px each side), icon-to-label gap (6px), and typography (14px/400/20px line-height) were IDENTICAL across every row type and every nesting depth — fully aligned, no divergence. Width naturally varies by depth (less available space as indentation compounds), which is expected, not a bug. ONE genuine but invisible inconsistency found: the disabled leaf row (“Yearly”, a plain <div>, not a real Button) had zero vertical padding, relying solely on `items-center` + a fixed `h-9` height for centering, while every real Button row carries `py-2` (8px) inherited from Button's own base recipe (never overridden). Confirmed via screenshot this had ZERO visible effect — flexbox centering inside a fixed height keeps content vertically centered identically regardless of the padding value underneath — but the underlying CSS values genuinely didn't match. Normalized by adding explicit `py-2` to the disabled row's className so its computed padding is identical to every other row, not merely visually equivalent. Verified via getComputedStyle (paddingTop/Bottom now 8px, matching) and screenshot (pixel-identical rendering before and after).

rows.title: First genuinely exhaustive, AI-initiated sweep of the whole component (not prompted by a specific visible symptom) — found one real dead-code issue in seconds
rows.detail: Prompted by “we have detected many divergences even though we suppose to respect the fact that we can only use native primitives/components... we need to refine the protocol for this sandbox factory line to reduce this to zero.” Rather than only writing new policy prose, ran a genuinely exhaustive, scripted audit of every Button/Input/DropdownMenu usage in FunctionalRailSidebar.tsx RIGHT NOW: every className override checked against its target primitive's real base recipe via `twMerge()` run directly (not by inspection), every interactive state (hover/press/disabled) verified via live event simulation + getComputedStyle, not assumed from source. RESULT: every className merge was clean (RailIconButton, overflow trigger, leaf/group Buttons, DropdownMenuContent width overrides, PanelBadge, InputGroup — all confirmed via twMerge to have zero leftover conflicting base classes) and every interactive state fired correctly (Panel actions/Collapse sidebar buttons, never explicitly tested before this pass, correctly hover from transparent to oklch(0.97 0 0)). ONE genuine issue found: the disabled “Profile” button still carried a leftover `hover:bg-transparent` — confirmed via `:matches(':hover')` (returns false even under a forced hover attempt) that Button's own `disabled:pointer-events-none` makes hover permanently unreachable on a disabled element, so the override was syntactically correct (twMerge confirmed it does replace the base `hover:bg-accent`) but 100% functionally dead. Removed it — not because it caused a visible bug, but because leftover code that closely mimics the M-12 anti-pattern (a hover override with no real purpose) is exactly the kind of thing that misleads a future maintainer into thinking suppression is intentionally needed. This is the FIRST time in the entire Rail Sidebar transformation that an issue was found by an AI-initiated systematic sweep rather than a human noticing something and asking about it — documented here specifically to serve as the evidence that CLAUDE.md's new mandatory “Primitive Fidelity Checklist” (added in this same turn) actually catches things reactive, one-at-a-time review misses. See LIMBO-PROTOCOL-LOG.md's flaws log for the full retrospective and the Agent Roster update making this checklist mandatory for the Build agent, not deferred entirely to the separate (and, until now, never-invoked) Independent Audit agent.

rows.title: Panel container had no border, even though it behaves exactly like a menu/popover (mounts on trigger, floats over content, dismisses) — explicit user instruction, not an AI-initiated proposal
rows.detail: Prompted directly: “lets start with adding a border to apply the container characteristics of menus to the sidebar as it is considered almost like one because when a button from the rail is clicked then it appears.” Checked origin's real source first (design-system/src/gallery/RailNav.tsx): the PANEL itself (~line 810) has NO border at all — only `boxShadow: elev.mid`, an elevation shadow, with an explicit code comment calling out a deliberate overflow:hidden/visible dance just to keep that shadow from being clipped during the open/close width animation. Origin's SEPARATE overflow/“More” dropdown menu (~line 1717–1723, a genuinely different element) DOES carry a real border (`border: 1px solid ${tokens.hairline}`), with its own code comment: “KEPT (owner ruling 2026-07-20): DS menu-definition convention... Figma has no stroke, but we keep a hairline for legibility on light surfaces.” So origin itself treats “panel” and “menu” as two different container recipes (shadow-only vs. bordered) — the request here is a deliberate bidezine-specific decision to instead treat them as the SAME kind of container, which is a legitimate design call (this panel functionally IS a dismissible, trigger-opened overlay, i.e. a menu/popover in every behavioral sense), not a copy of origin's panel styling. Checked bidezine's own real DropdownMenuContent recipe for what “menu container characteristics” actually means here: `rounded-md border bg-popover ... shadow-md` (src/ui/dropdown-menu.tsx) — the plain `border` utility, which this repo's Tailwind `@theme` wiring (src/styles/system.css: `--color-border: var(--border)`) resolves to the exact same `--border` token already bound to `colors.hairline` in this file (used for the header's own divider line). Applied a `1px solid ${colors.hairline}` border to the panel's outer container, reusing that already-established token rather than inventing a new one. No shadow was added in this pass — only the border, per the user's own explicit “let's start with” framing (a second, separate issue is expected next).

rows.title: Panel was missing the rest of the menu recipe: the shadow/elevation token and the open/close animations — explicit follow-up instruction, not an AI-initiated proposal
rows.detail: Prompted directly: “it is not just the border you need to emulate everything from the menu... the elevation token, the animations.” Extended L-15's reasoning to the rest of the real DropdownMenuContent recipe (src/ui/dropdown-menu.tsx: `rounded-md border bg-popover p-1 text-popover-foreground shadow-md data-[side=...]:slide-in-from-* data-[state=closed]:animate-out data-[state=closed]:fade-out-0 data-[state=closed]:zoom-out-95 data-[state=open]:animate-in data-[state=open]:fade-in-0 data-[state=open]:zoom-in-95`). Added `shadow-md` verbatim (a plain Tailwind utility, no bidezine-specific --shadow-* token exists to diverge from — confirmed via getComputedStyle the rendered box-shadow is byte-identical to the real DropdownMenuContent's own). Deliberately did NOT copy `z-50`/`min-w-[8rem]`/`max-h-(--radix-dropdown-menu-content-available-height)`/`origin-(--radix-dropdown-menu-content-transform-origin)`/the `slide-in-from-*` variants — all of those depend on Radix Popper's floating/portal positioning (a measured `data-side` attribute and available-height custom property), which doesn't apply here: this panel is laid out in-flow next to the rail, not a floating overlay positioned relative to a trigger. For the animation classes, the harder problem was the exit animation: a plain `{openSection && <div>}` conditional unmounts synchronously the instant `openSection` goes null, giving the `fade-out-0`/`zoom-out-95`/`animate-out` classes zero time to actually play. Rather than hand-roll a `setTimeout`-based unmount delay (which would be exactly the kind of reinvented, ad-hoc mechanism this session has repeatedly flagged as wrong), added `@radix-ui/react-presence` (v1.1.10, matching the version already resolved transitively via the existing `@radix-ui/react-dropdown-menu` dependency) as a genuine, explicit dependency of limbo-factory's own package.json — this is the exact real primitive every actual Radix Content component (Popover/DropdownMenu/Dialog) uses internally to solve this precise problem, confirmed by reading their own compiled source (`@radix-ui/react-dialog`'s DialogContent literally does `<Presence present={forceMount || context.open}>{content}</Presence>`, and derives `data-state` directly from `context.open`, NOT from Presence's own render-prop — the initial attempt here used the function/render-prop child form and hit a real type error, since Presence's forceMount branch (active for that form) requires a real element back, not `null`; switched to the plain-element form to match real Radix usage exactly). Also added a `displaySection` (last-known-non-null `openSection`, updated synchronously during render via a ref, not useEffect, to avoid a one-tick lag) so the header/tree content stays visible and populated while Presence holds the wrapper mounted for the exit animation — `openSection` itself goes `undefined` the instant closing starts, which would otherwise blank the panel's content a frame before the animation had a chance to play. VERIFIED, not assumed: getComputedStyle confirmed the panel's rendered `boxShadow` is byte-identical to the real DropdownMenuContent's; live interaction confirmed `data-state`/`animationName` genuinely read `open`/`enter` on open and `closed`/`exit` on close (the element staying mounted mid-fade, opacity mid-transition, not instantly gone); a `Presence`-usage mistake (function-child form) was caught by `tsc`, not shipped. Also investigated and ruled OUT as unrelated: an intermittent `"Attempted to synchronously unmount a root while React was already rendering"` console error — confirmed via `git stash`/rebuild that this reproduces identically on the untouched pre-L-16 baseline purely from switching the page's own Origin/Adjusted tabs (which mounts/unmounts an iframe hosting the vendored origin component), with zero dependency on this change or the panel's open/close cycle at all; not fixed here as it's a pre-existing, out-of-scope issue in the limbo-factory preview harness itself, not in FunctionalRailSidebar.tsx.

Deliberately did NOT copy `z-50`/`min-w-[8rem]`/`max-h-(--radix-dropdown-menu-content-available-height)`/`origin-(--radix-dropdown-menu-content-transform-origin)`/the `slide-in-from-*` variants — all of those depend on Radix Popper's floating/portal positioning (a measured `data-side` attribute and available-height custom property), which doesn't apply here: this panel is laid out in-flow next to the rail, not a floating overlay positioned relative to a trigger. For the animation classes, the harder problem was the exit animation: a plain `{openSection && <div>}` conditional unmounts synchronously the instant `openSection` goes null, giving the `fade-out-0`/`zoom-out-95`/`animate-out` classes zero time to actually play. Rather than hand-roll a `setTimeout`-based unmount delay (which would be exactly the kind of reinvented, ad-hoc mechanism this session has repeatedly flagged as wrong), added `@radix-ui/react-presence` (v1.1.10, matching the version already resolved transitively via the existing `@radix-ui/react-dropdown-menu` dependency) as a genuine, explicit dependency of limbo-factory's own package.json — this is the exact real primitive every actual Radix Content component (Popover/DropdownMenu/Dialog) uses internally to solve this precise problem, confirmed by reading their own compiled source (`@radix-ui/react-dialog`'s DialogContent literally does `<Presence present={forceMount || context.open}>{content}</Presence>`, and derives `data-state` directly from `context.open`, NOT from Presence's own render-prop — the initial attempt here used the function/render-prop child form and hit a real type error, since Presence's forceMount branch (active for that form) requires a real element back, not `null`; switched to the plain-element form to match real Radix usage exactly). Also added a `displaySection` (last-known-non-null `openSection`, updated synchronously during render via a ref, not useEffect, to avoid a one-tick lag) so the header/tree content stays visible and populated while Presence holds the wrapper mounted for the exit animation — `openSection` itself goes `undefined` the instant closing starts, which would otherwise blank the panel's content a frame before the animation had a chance to play. VERIFIED, not assumed: getComputedStyle confirmed the panel's rendered `boxShadow` is byte-identical to the real DropdownMenuContent's; live interaction confirmed `data-state`/`animationName` genuinely read `open`/`enter` on open and `closed`/`exit` on close (the element staying mounted mid-fade, opacity mid-transition, not instantly gone); a `Presence`-usage mistake (function-child form) was caught by `tsc`, not shipped. Also investigated and ruled OUT as unrelated: an intermittent `"Attempted to synchronously unmount a root while React was already rendering"` console error — confirmed via `git stash`/rebuild that this reproduces identically on the untouched pre-L-16 baseline purely from switching the page's own Origin/Adjusted tabs (which mounts/unmounts an iframe hosting the vendored origin component), with zero dependency on this change or the panel's open/close cycle at all; not fixed here as it's a pre-existing, out-of-scope issue in the limbo-factory preview harness itself, not in FunctionalRailSidebar.tsx.

rows.title: PanelTree group-toggle rows put the chevron on the LEFT and had no content icon at all — copied straight from origin's own layout, never checked against bidezine's own real chevron conventions; 6 group nodes (system-logic, schedules, products, orders, sales, customers) were silently missing the icon field origin's own SPEC_TREE always has
rows.detail: Prompted directly: “the chevron icon in the sidebar menu that shows expansion and collapse is located in the left side while our sidebar locates it to the far right, thats not acceptable because it diverges from the protocol... the options that allow to expand and collapse are missing their icons.” Checked origin's real source (design-system/src/gallery/RailNav.tsx ~line 1487-1501): its own PanelItem row renders the chevron slot FIRST, before the nav-icon slot — our earlier port (L-9) copied that ordering wholesale without separately checking it against bidezine's OWN real chevron conventions. Checked bidezine's own two real “expand/collapse with a chevron” primitives: AccordionTrigger (src/ui/accordion.tsx) renders `{children}` first, `<ChevronDownIcon>` LAST, inside a `justify-between` row; DropdownMenuSubTrigger/ContextMenuSubTrigger/MenubarSubTrigger all place `ChevronRightIcon` last with `ml-auto`. Both put the chevron at the FAR RIGHT, never the left — confirming the user's exact complaint and identifying it as an origin-layout contamination, not a bidezine convention. Separately, GroupNode (the type for group-toggle rows) had NO `icon` field at all, unlike LeafItem — confirmed this was an incomplete port, not deliberate: origin's SPEC_TREE gives every group its own Icon (IconCubeTree for “System logic”, IconCalendarClock for “Schedules”, IconGrid/IconCart/IconMoney/IconPeople for Products/Orders/Sales/Customers in the Documents panel), and CartIcon/GridIcon/MoneyIcon were ALREADY imported into this file but never referenced anywhere — dead imports left over from an unfinished step. FULL_PREVIEW_ICONS already had cubeTree/calendarClock entries defined (fluent slugs cube_tree_20_regular / calendar_clock_20_regular, both verified to exist in @fluentui/svg-icons, exact matches to origin's own icon choices) but never wired into the SLIDES_PANEL data. FIXED: added `icon` to GroupNode; populated all 6 groups (system-logic→cubeTree, schedules→calendarClock, products→GridIcon, orders→CartIcon, sales→MoneyIcon, customers→PeopleIcon, the last newly imported); restructured the group row to icon-first/label/badge/chevron-last, the exact same order as a leaf row with only the chevron appended — the label's own `flex-1` already pushes the badge and chevron hard against the row's right edge (the same mechanism that already positioned the badge correctly), so no extra `ml-auto` was needed. Verified via screenshot in both the Slides and Documents panels: every group now shows its own content icon on the left and the chevron on the far right, matching bidezine's real Accordion/DropdownMenuSub convention exactly.

rows.title: Panel's ScrollArea ignored the container's own padding and left no gap between content and the scrollbar — confirmed via measurement as a genuine NEGATIVE gap (content overlapped by the scrollbar thumb), not just a subjective closeness. FOLLOW-UP (L-21): the first fix only addressed the content-to-scrollbar gap, not the scrollbar-to-panel-edge gap the user's screenshot showed was still broken
rows.detail: Prompted directly: “the rail nav from the origin has a more efficient way to handle the scroll bar by allocating it in a layout component with the group it belongs to, respecting the container's padding and adding a proper gap between the scrolling area and the content. the one proposed in the adjusted ignores the container's padding and there is no gap between the content, making it too close.” Measured live BEFORE changing anything: with the scrollbar thumb actually visible (forced via a real wheel-scroll), the tree content's own right edge sat at x=1128.2 while the scrollbar track's left edge sat at x=1124.2 — a NEGATIVE 4px gap, i.e. genuine overlap. Root cause: Radix ScrollArea's own ScrollBar is an absolutely-positioned overlay (a sibling of Viewport inside Root), not a flex sibling that reserves layout space, so it floats on top of whatever sits at the Viewport's right edge — this content div's `p-1.5` (6px uniform) was never enough to clear the 10px-wide scrollbar track (src/ui/scroll-area.tsx: `w-2.5`). Read origin's own real documentation and source before changing anything (design-system/docs/atomic/atom/scrollbar.spec.md + design-system/src/gallery/RailNav.tsx): origin's real technique is a documented “two-layer scroll region” (their own comment: “NavPanelShell FRAME — two-layer scroll. Outer shell owns padding (SPACE[2]) + overflow:hidden + flex column; inner <nav> owns the scroll (overflowY:auto, flex:1, minHeight:0)”), plus a documented “figma-artifact-gap-translation” rule: “when a molecule/organism uses this Scrollbar as a sibling to a scroll container, the gap: 8px in Figma between the scroll content and the scrollbar translates to paddingRight: SPACE[2] on the content element (not a separate gap).” Origin's inner <nav> carries `paddingRight: navScrollable ? SPACE[2] : 0` — an EXTRA right-side gutter reserved specifically for the scrollbar, on top of the outer shell's own uniform padding, applied only when content is actually scrollable. FIRST FIX (later found incomplete, see L-21): changed the content div's `p-1.5` to `p-1.5 pr-4`, fixing the content-to-scrollbar gap (-4px → +6px) — but the claim that “Radix's ScrollArea Root already plays the outer shell role... so no extra wrapper div was needed” was WRONG; see L-21 for the corrected, complete fix (an actual outer padded shell wrapping ScrollArea). BROADER QUESTION, explicitly not auto-decided: the user asked whether this two-layer outer-padding/inner-scrollbar-gutter concept should be extended into bidezine's own real ScrollArea-consuming components system-wide (DropdownMenuContent, Select, Command, ContextMenu, Menubar, NavigationMenu, Sidebar, etc.), not just this rail panel — a genuine wide-blast-radius architecture change to the REAL shipped design system, surfaced back to the user rather than auto-applied.

rows.title: Real DropdownMenuItem primitive has no truncate/whitespace-nowrap by default — a long rail section label in the overflow “More” menu would wrap onto a second line instead of ellipsis-truncating
rows.detail: Prompted by “the text in each option should truncate if its too long, text wrap is not allowed.” Audited every text-bearing row in FunctionalRailSidebar.tsx: PanelTree leaf/disabled-leaf/group rows already all had `truncate` on their label spans (confirmed via getComputedStyle: whiteSpace:nowrap, overflow:hidden, textOverflow:ellipsis on all three, verified live against the longest real labels in the data — “Customer satisfaction”, “Sport and fitness” — no wrapping in any case), and the panel header title already had `truncate` (D-11). The ONE genuine gap found: the real DropdownMenuItem primitive (src/ui/dropdown-menu.tsx) carries no truncate/whitespace-nowrap/overflow-hidden anywhere in its own base recipe — a plain text child has no width constraint or overflow handling at all, so a long enough rail section label in the overflow “More” menu would wrap rather than truncate. Scoped the fix to this call site only — wrapping the label in its own `min-w-0 flex-1 truncate` span — rather than editing the shared primitive itself, since DropdownMenuItem is used everywhere across the real design system and changing its base recipe is a wider decision than this rail component's own scope covers. Verified via getComputedStyle after the fix: whiteSpace:nowrap/overflow:hidden/textOverflow:ellipsis all correctly applied on the overflow menu's item labels. BROADER QUESTION, explicitly not auto-decided: should every real menu-item-style primitive (DropdownMenuItem/ContextMenuItem/MenubarItem/CommandItem, etc.) gain this truncation by default system-wide, matching the same scope question raised by L-18's scrollbar finding — surfaced back to the user rather than auto-applied.

rows.title: RailButtonDark
rows.detail: VISUAL MODEL now resolved: rather than adding a new dark-rail variant to buttonVariants, RailIconButton composes the real Button as-is (`variant="ghost" size="icon"`) and drives its dark-rail-specific background/foreground purely through inline `style` overrides sourced from the approved dark-rail color tokens (colors.hover/pressed/active/fg/fgHover/fgSubtle) — no shadcn variant addition needed, and no light-surface bleed-through, confirmed visually (“rail seems right entirely”). BEHAVIOR requirement (verified against design-system/src/gallery/RailButtonDark.tsx): showTooltip = (hovered || focused) && !isBrowsing && !isActive && !isDisabled — the hover tooltip must be SUPPRESSED once a rail button is active (selected) or browsing (its panel is open), not shown unconditionally on hover. Implemented and interactively verified in the limbo-factory preview build: RailIconButton skips the Tooltip wrapper entirely for active/browsing states (do NOT implement this by toggling Radix Tooltip's `open` prop between `false`/`undefined` — that flips the component between controlled/uncontrolled and triggers a React warning, confirmed via manual testing).

rows.title: Some Fluent regular→filled icon pairs (video, video_settings) have such drastically different silhouettes that hovering reads as “swapping to a different icon,” not “filling in the same icon” — confirmed genuine and NOT a bidezine bug
rows.detail: Prompted by “there are some icons that when hovering instead of changing to the fill form it swaps the icon with other one.” Investigated empirically rather than reasoning from raw SVG path text: rendered before/after hover screenshots for every icon actually used in this component (Activity stream/video, Live operations/video_settings, Rules engine/engine, Triggers/arrow_sync_off, Participants/people_community, Content/content_view, Daily/document, plus the real bidezine Grid/Cart/Money/People icons now used for group rows). RESULT: most pairs fill gracefully and read as “the same icon, filled in” (Participants, Daily, Rules engine, Triggers, all 4 real bidezine group icons — confirmed by direct visual comparison, not assumption). TWO clear, confirmed offenders: “Activity stream” (video) and “Live operations” (video_settings) — their filled forms are dramatic simplifications (video's line-art camera-with-viewfinder becomes a plain solid rounded rectangle; video_settings' gear overlay disappears from the filled form entirely), reading as a genuinely different pictogram to the eye, not a filled version of the same one. Cross-checked against the REAL Fluent source directly (node_modules/@fluentui/svg-icons/icons/video_20_filled.svg): our `filledD` path is byte-identical to Microsoft's own real Fluent filled glyph — this is not a bidezine data error or a miscopied path, it is genuinely how Fluent's own design renders this specific icon's filled state. Asked the user directly which of three remedies to apply (accept as-is / exempt from hover-fill / choose different icons); the user was unavailable to respond at the time, so the most conservative, fully reversible option was applied provisionally — (b), removing `filledD` from both entries so specTreeIcon's own fallback (`filled && entry.filledD ? entry.filledD : entry.d`) always rendered the regular glyph regardless of the `filled` prop, leaving this row's status as “decision,” not “resolved.” FINAL RESOLUTION (see L-27): that provisional exemption was itself reported back as a bug (“many icons are not filling”) once the user noticed the inconsistency directly — two icons behaving differently from every other actionable icon in the same component reads as broken, not as a deliberate design choice, regardless of the underlying Fluent-fidelity rationale. Resolved via option (a): both icons now fill on hover/press/select like every other actionable icon, using their real, verified Fluent filled paths (re-read directly from node_modules/@fluentui/svg-icons/icons/ rather than reconstructed from memory — see L-27 for why that distinction mattered). The visual jump from line-art to solid shape is accepted as correct Fluent behavior, matching Q1's system-wide rule with zero carved-out exceptions.

rows.title: L-18's fix was incomplete: it only cleared the gap between tree CONTENT and the scrollbar, never gave the scrollbar itself any clearance from the panel's own outer edge — the scrollbar thumb still sat flush (0.8px) against the panel's border, exactly as the user's follow-up screenshot showed. FOLLOW-UP (L-22): this fix's own first attempt then created a NEW regression — the scroll region touched t
rows.detail: Prompted directly, with a screenshot: “the scrollbar still ignoring the padding of the sidebar container. why didn't you fix this?” Measured before touching anything (not assumed from the screenshot alone): with the scrollbar visible via a real scroll, the gap between the scrollbar's own right edge and the panel's outer border was 0.8px — essentially flush, confirming the screenshot. Root cause of why L-18's fix didn't reach this: L-18 only added padding to the CONTENT div sitting inside ScrollArea's Viewport — it never gave ScrollArea itself (and therefore the scrollbar glued to Root's own edge) any clearance from the panel's true outer border, because the panel container had zero padding around ScrollArea on any side. Investigated why simply adding padding to ScrollArea's own Root wouldn't have worked either, before implementing anything: read @radix-ui/react-scroll-area's compiled source directly and confirmed ScrollAreaScrollbar is positioned `position: absolute; right: 0` relative to Root's own padding box — an absolutely positioned `right: 0` child sits flush with its containing block's padding-box edge regardless of THAT SAME element's own padding value, so padding added directly to Root would never have pushed the scrollbar inward. Only a SEPARATE wrapping element's padding, sitting outside ScrollArea's own box entirely, can create real clearance. FIRST ATTEMPT (later found incomplete, see L-22): wrapped ScrollArea in a new shell div carrying `px-2 pb-2` (8px, horizontal + bottom only) and moved the `flex-1 overflow-hidden` (K-3's flex-sizing fix) from ScrollArea onto this new wrapper — ScrollArea itself now just fills it (`size-full`). Verified via getBoundingClientRect after the fix: the gap between the scrollbar and the panel's outer edge was now 8.8px (was 0.8px), the content-to-scrollbar gap from L-18 was still correctly 6px (unaffected), and scrolling was re-verified to genuinely work. Screenshot-confirmed in light mode. This fixed the reported bug but, per L-22, introduced a new one (missing top padding) in the same change. Self-critical note, in the same spirit as prior findings this session: L-18's original detail text explicitly asserted Radix's ScrollArea Root already served as the “outer shell” and that no wrapper div was needed — that claim was accepted without measuring the ACTUAL distance from the scrollbar to the panel's own outer border (only the content-to-scrollbar distance was measured), so an incomplete fix was documented as if it were complete. The lesson is the same one already captured in CLAUDE.md checklist item 14 (added this session): a decorative/overlay element's geometric footprint must be measured against ALL of its relevant neighbors — here, both the immediate content AND the outer container boundary — not just the one neighbor the original bug report happened to mention.

Investigated why simply adding padding to ScrollArea's own Root wouldn't have worked either, before implementing anything: read @radix-ui/react-scroll-area's compiled source directly and confirmed ScrollAreaScrollbar is positioned `position: absolute; right: 0` relative to Root's own padding box — an absolutely positioned `right: 0` child sits flush with its containing block's padding-box edge regardless of THAT SAME element's own padding value, so padding added directly to Root would never have pushed the scrollbar inward. Only a SEPARATE wrapping element's padding, sitting outside ScrollArea's own box entirely, can create real clearance. FIRST ATTEMPT (later found incomplete, see L-22): wrapped ScrollArea in a new shell div carrying `px-2 pb-2` (8px, horizontal + bottom only) and moved the `flex-1 overflow-hidden` (K-3's flex-sizing fix) from ScrollArea onto this new wrapper — ScrollArea itself now just fills it (`size-full`). Verified via getBoundingClientRect after the fix: the gap between the scrollbar and the panel's outer edge was now 8.8px (was 0.8px), the content-to-scrollbar gap from L-18 was still correctly 6px (unaffected), and scrolling was re-verified to genuinely work. Screenshot-confirmed in light mode. This fixed the reported bug but, per L-22, introduced a new one (missing top padding) in the same change. Self-critical note, in the same spirit as prior findings this session: L-18's original detail text explicitly asserted Radix's ScrollArea Root already served as the “outer shell” and that no wrapper div was needed — that claim was accepted without measuring the ACTUAL distance from the scrollbar to the panel's own outer border (only the content-to-scrollbar distance was measured), so an incomplete fix was documented as if it were complete. The lesson is the same one already captured in CLAUDE.md checklist item 14 (added this session): a decorative/overlay element's geometric footprint must be measured against ALL of its relevant neighbors — here, both the immediate content AND the outer container boundary — not just the one neighbor the original bug report happened to mention.

rows.title: L-21's own new wrapper shell used asymmetric padding (`px-2 pb-2`, no top) instead of matching origin's real uniform padding-on-all-sides convention — fixed the scrollbar-to-edge gap but immediately created a new regression: the scroll region touched the search box directly above it
rows.detail: Prompted directly: “now it is not respecting the gap between elements, it is now touching the search bar, where it's supposed to have a gap between them. did you analyze how the origin manages these components in a layout manner?” This was a fair challenge — the honest answer was no, not thoroughly enough: L-21's own investigation had focused entirely on the SCROLLBAR-specific comment thread (the “figma-artifact-gap-translation” rule about paddingRight) and never re-read origin's actual, complete layout declaration for the wrapping shell itself. Went back and read origin's real source properly this time (design-system/src/gallery/RailNav.tsx ~lines 913-1013, the full region from the header divider through the NavPanelShell): origin's real “NavPanelShell FRAME” wrapper is declared as a SINGLE property, `padding: ${SPACE[2]}px` — a uniform padding shorthand applied to all four sides (top included), not an asymmetric horizontal+bottom-only pairing. L-21's own wrapper only copied the bottom/horizontal sides that had come up in the scrollbar-gutter discussion and never re-verified the padding declaration's actual shape against origin's one-line source before shipping. FIXED: changed the wrapper's className from `px-2 pb-2` to a plain `p-2`, matching origin's uniform-padding-on-all-sides convention exactly. Verified via getBoundingClientRect after the fix: the gap between the search box's bottom edge and the first tree row's top edge is now 12px (was effectively 0, confirmed touching before the fix), while the scrollbar-to-panel-edge gap from L-21 is unaffected (still 8.8px) and scrolling still genuinely works (scrollTop advances on a real wheel event). Also noted, not implemented (flagged rather than silently added as a new visual element without confirmation): origin's real structure additionally places a `0.5px` hairline divider line between the search bar and the NavPanelShell — a distinct visual separator, not just spacing — which our version currently omits, relying on padding alone for that boundary. The header's own existing divider (`borderBottom`, already an approved pattern in this same file) is available to reuse for this if the user wants that reinforced later. Lesson for the standing checklist: measuring one neighbor relationship correctly (L-21's scrollbar-to-edge gap) does not verify a different neighbor relationship on the same element (the wrapper's OWN top edge against the sibling above it) — every side of a repositioned/repadded element needs its own explicit measurement, not just the side the immediate bug report was about.

rows.title: ROOT CAUSE FOUND for a recurring class of “icon doesn't fill on hover/select” reports (the user's fifth time flagging this): specTreeIcon-based icons silently stop filling entirely in a PRODUCTION build, while real generated icons keep working in the exact same bundle — a genuine, previously-undiscovered, deployment-risk bug, not another isolated icon mismatch
rows.detail: Prompted by: “this is the fifth time that icon are not filling when hovering or selected, and some icons are not even the same icon type when hovering or selecting, this is serious because it shows there is a fundamental issue in the code that keeps breaking this, and we run the risk that this issue will pass to deployment for future projects.” Took this literally rather than patching another one-off icon: ran an exhaustive hover sweep across every icon in the rail (rail buttons, Slides panel, Documents panel) against the live dev server first — found no NEW visual mismatches beyond the already-fixed/exempted video/video_settings pair (L-20); one apparent failure (“Content”) turned out to be a test-methodology artifact (the row's layout position was below the actual browser viewport height, so the mouse was never really landing on it — confirmed by properly scrolling it into view and re-testing, at which point it filled correctly like everything else). Since no further isolated bug was found, investigated the MECHANISM itself instead: src/lib/action-icons.tsx's `isIconElement()` has two detection paths — an explicit `isActionIcon === true` marker set on every real generated icon (scripts/build-icons.mjs), and a fallback matching `.name`/`.displayName` against `endsWith("Icon")`, with the file's OWN code comment already warning the fallback is unsafe under production minification (“bundlers like Rollup/esbuild routinely rename function declarations during tree-shaking/scope hoisting”). specTreeIcon's returned component relied SOLELY on that unsafe fallback (declared as `function SpecIcon(...)`, no marker). PROVED this empirically, not just theoretically: ran `npm run build`, confirmed via direct string search that the minified bundle contains zero occurrences of “SpecIcon” (the name is gone) while “isActionIcon” survives (a property-name string reference, not a renamed identifier); then served the actual built dist/ output (`npm run preview`) and tested hover live — confirmed every specTreeIcon-based icon (“Participants”, “Rules engine”, etc.) had COMPLETELY STOPPED filling on hover/select, with zero console errors, a fully silent failure, while a real generated icon in the identical bundle (“Documents”) still worked correctly. This is the actual, fundamental root cause behind the recurring pattern: every fix made across this whole session (this turn's and prior ones') was verified only against the Vite DEV SERVER, where function names survive — so a component-wide regression was shipping invisibly underneath passing dev-server checks every single time; the dev server itself was never a valid test environment for this specific failure mode. FIXED at the source, not per-icon: added `SpecIcon.isActionIcon = true` as a static property on the returned component, mirroring exactly how the real generated-icon pipeline marks its own output — immune to minification regardless of what name the closure ends up with. VERIFIED against the actual rebuilt production bundle (not just re-read as fixed): re-ran the identical build+preview+hover-live test and confirmed every specTreeIcon-based icon across both the Slides and Documents panels (Participants, Rules engine, Triggers, Apps, Products, Orders, plus every top-level rail icon: Gauge, Globe, Flag, Gift, Graduation, Images) now fills correctly in the production build, matching real generated icons exactly. Added a new, durable safeguard to CLAUDE.md's Primitive Fidelity Checklist (item 15) specifically: anything relying on a component's runtime `.name`/`.displayName` identity must be verified against an actual production/minified build, not only the dev server — aimed directly at preventing this exact class of silent, deployment-only regression from recurring in any future project.

rows.title: RailIconButton (the top-level rail nav buttons) only filled its icon on isActive||isBrowsing — hover alone never filled it, contradicting Q1's own resolved decision that hover is one of the three fill-triggering states. cubeTree/calendarClock (System logic/Schedules group icons) were ALSO silently non-responsive to any fill state, for a different reason: both FULL_PREVIEW_ICONS entries had no fill
rows.detail: Prompted directly, with a report that the rail sidebar “still having the same issue seen this morning.” First measurement was misleading: an early hover test on “Documents” appeared to show the icon correctly filling, contradicting a direct read of RailIconButton's own source (`filled={isActive || isBrowsing}`, no `isHovered`). Re-tested cleanly after a fresh reload with the layout's own ResizeObserver-driven pinned/stashed recalculation fully settled (the initial paint transiently renders ALL 15 rail sections before the observer trims it down to the pinned set + overflow menu, and the earlier test had coincided with that transient window) — confirmed definitively: `filled` genuinely never changes on pure hover for any rail-level button. Checked origin's real RailButtonDark.tsx directly: `filled={!isDisabled && (isActive || isBrowsing || isHovered || isPressed)}` — hover and press both count, confirming this was a genuine regression, not a deliberate scope reduction. FIXED: added `isHovered || isPressed` to RailIconButton's own fill condition, matching origin exactly. SEPARATELY, while sweeping every rail/panel icon for the same defect class, found “System logic” and “Schedules” (group-toggle rows, not leaf rows) never filled on ANY state, including hover — even though the leaf rows around them (Rules engine, Triggers, Daily, Content) all correctly fill via the real Button primitive's own built-in `useActionIconFill`/`fillActionIcons` wiring (src/ui/button.tsx), which these group rows also compose. Root cause was NOT the fill mechanism (that part works identically for both) but the DATA: `FULL_PREVIEW_ICONS.cubeTree`/`.calendarClock` (rail-sidebar.ts) had only a `d` (regular) field, no `filledD` — unlike L-20's video/video_settings, this had NO documented exemption comment, and checking origin's real IconCubeTree/IconCalendarClock (design-system/src/icons/fluent.tsx) confirmed BOTH genuinely have a distinct, real filled variant in the origin source — this was a straightforward, undocumented porting gap, not a deliberate design decision. FIXED: added the real `filledD` values, copied verbatim from origin's own `IconCubeTree`/`IconCalendarClock` filled-branch paths. VERIFIED live in the browser (not assumed from the diff): re-tested hover on every rail button (all fill correctly now, including the previously-active “Slides”/“Monthly” items which correctly show no VISIBLE change since they're already filled at rest) and on System logic/Schedules specifically (both now fill on hover, confirmed via direct SVG `d` attribute comparison before/after). Re-verified in a rebuilt production bundle, not only the dev server, per the L-23 lesson.

rows.title: The two-layer scroll region's inner gutter (pe-2/pr-4) was applied UNCONDITIONALLY across every migrated component (src/ui/dropdown-menu.tsx, context-menu.tsx, command.tsx, combobox.tsx) and this rail panel's own tree — leaving dead empty space on the scrollbar's side any time content happened to fit without actually needing to scroll
rows.detail: Prompted directly: “when there is no scrolling experience, then the gap and the area should not apply, this work amazing in the other design system where the RailNav is coming from but in ours keeps failing.” Checked origin's real RailNav.tsx and found the exact mechanism already solving this: a `navScrollable` state (`el.scrollHeight > el.clientHeight`, re-checked via `ResizeObserver`) gates the inner gutter — `paddingRight: navScrollable ? SPACE[2] : 0` — with origin's own code explicitly naming the anti-pattern this guards against in a comment, `SC.UNCONDITIONAL-SCROLLBAR-GAP`. Our own migration (this session's earlier scroll-region work) never reproduced this conditional check — every migrated component's inner content wrapper carried a bare, always-on `pe-2` (or this panel's `pr-4`), regardless of whether ScrollArea's content actually overflowed. FIXED at the primitive level so every consumer benefits automatically, not per-component: `ScrollArea` (src/ui/scroll-area.tsx) now runs the identical `scrollHeight > clientHeight` (and `scrollWidth > clientWidth`) check itself via a `ResizeObserver` watching both its Viewport and the Viewport's own content, exposing the result as `data-scrollable-y`/`data-scrollable-x` on `Root` (which also gained a `group/scroll-area` class name for this purpose). Every migrated component's inner gutter was changed from a bare `pe-2`/`pr-4` to `group-data-[scrollable-y=true]/scroll-area:pe-2` (or `-pr-4` for this panel, matching its existing pixel value) — present only when `ScrollArea` itself reports real overflow. VERIFIED in both directions, live: (1) Combobox's 5-item “framework” list — genuinely fits (168px viewport, 168px content) — correctly shows `data-scrollable-y="false"` and only its base 4px padding, zero extra gutter; force-shrinking the same list's max-height flips it to `"true"` and the gutter reappears at 8px. (2) This rail panel's own tree: with “System logic” expanded (302px available vs 424px content, genuinely overflowing) `data-scrollable-y="true"` and the gutter is the full 16px (`p-1.5` base + `pr-4` override); collapsing that same group shrinks content to fit exactly (302=302) and the gutter correctly drops back to the base 6px with zero override. Folded into CLAUDE.md's Scroll region protocol as a permanent, mandatory third layer (conditional gutter) alongside the existing outer-padding and inner-gutter layers, with a two-directional verification requirement (confirm the gutter both appears AND disappears, not just one direction).

rows.title: L-25's own fix mechanism was itself broken: the `group-data-[scrollable-y=true]/scroll-area:pe-2` CSS selector matches ANY ancestor sharing the `group/scroll-area` class+attribute, not just the nearest one — since site/src/components/Layout.tsx wraps every page's <main> content in its own, almost-always-scrollable page-level ScrollArea, every nested component demo's conditional gutter was silently
rows.detail: Prompted directly, after the user reported seeing the exact same scrolling/gutter issues again despite L-25 being marked resolved: “I still see examples in the local host 4188 and I still see the same issues I am asking to fix broadly... something else to add is that when there is no scrolling experience, then the gap and the area should not apply, this works amazing in the other design system... but in ours keeps failing” and later “I am not sure what you are fixing but I still seeing the same issue in multiple places for both of the problems... I thought I was specific on using multiple agents to not rely on one approving things for the sake of approving.” Re-verified L-25's own claims from scratch rather than trusting the earlier resolved status: reproduced a case where `document.querySelector('[data-slot="scroll-area"]')`-style naive queries grab the WRONG element (Layout's own persistent nav sidebar, first in DOM order) — the same class of scoping mistake a dispatched independent audit agent also made in its own findings. After re-scoping queries correctly (`.closest()` from a known specific descendant), found command.tsx's CommandList genuinely NOT scrollable (`data-scrollable-y="false"`, content 265=265) yet its inner gutter div still carried a real, measured 8px `paddingRight` — contradicting L-25's own "resolved" claim. ROOT CAUSE, found by inspecting the actual compiled Tailwind output directly (not just re-reading the source): `group-data-[scrollable-y=true]/scroll-area:pe-2` compiles to `:is(:where(.group\/scroll-area)[data-scrollable-y=true] *)` — a plain CSS descendant combinator matching ANY ancestor with that class+attribute, not specifically the nearest one. Every ScrollArea instance shares the identical `group/scroll-area` class name, and site/src/components/Layout.tsx's own page-level ScrollArea (wrapping literally every page's <main> content, and itself almost always scrollable) is a genuine ancestor of every component demo on the site — so its `scrollableY=true` state leaked into every nested, functionally-unrelated ScrollArea's conditional gutter, meaning the gutter was effectively always-on site-wide, silently defeating L-25's entire fix everywhere except limbo-factory (which has no such nested-ScrollArea-in-ScrollArea structure and so never exhibited the bug, explaining why it looked fixed there while failing on the real site). FIXED at the primitive level: replaced the CSS `group`/`data-*` selector mechanism in src/ui/scroll-area.tsx with a React Context (`ScrollAreaOverflowContext`, provided by ScrollArea around its own children inside Viewport, consumed via a new exported `useScrollAreaOverflow()` hook) — React Context always resolves to the NEAREST enclosing Provider regardless of naming collisions, which is exactly the semantics this needs. Removed the now-misleading `group/scroll-area` class from Root entirely (kept the `data-scrollable-y`/`data-scrollable-x` DOM attributes themselves, for tests/debugging only — no longer meant to drive styling via CSS selectors). Migrated all 6 real consumers from the CSS variant to the hook: src/ui/command.tsx (split into CommandList + CommandListInner so the hook is called from a component actually rendered inside ScrollArea's own children), src/ui/combobox.tsx (ComboboxList/ComboboxListInner, same split), src/ui/dropdown-menu.tsx (DropdownMenuScrollGutter), src/ui/context-menu.tsx (ContextMenuScrollGutter), limbo-factory/src/components/FunctionalRailSidebar.tsx (PanelTreeScrollGutter), and limbo-factory/src/App.tsx (PlaceholderPhaseGutter and a new QuadrantScrollGutter for QuadrantLayout's own left column, which had NO gutter at all before this pass — a separate, previously-unaudited Defect-A-adjacent gap found while sweeping every ScrollArea usage in the factory line itself, per the user's explicit instruction to apply this fix to ‘the entire bidezine system... and as well apply it to the limbo factory line’). site/src/components/Layout.tsx's own nav sidebar gutter (`data-[scrollable-y=true]:pr-2`, a SELF-referencing data-attribute selector, not a `group`-based one) was re-verified rather than assumed safe — confirmed it remains correct post-refactor since Root still carries its own `data-scrollable-y` attribute directly. rows.title: For the FIFTH reported time, icons in the rail sidebar were found not filling on hover/press/select — root cause was L-20's own provisional exemption of `video`/`videoSettings` (Activity stream / Live operations) never being escalated to a final decision, left silently sitting as the two icons in the entire sidebar with no fill behavior at all while every other icon around them correctly filled
rows.detail: Prompted directly: “in the sidebar there are many icon that ARE NOT filling when hovering, press, selecting, this is the fifth time i request to fix it... something that brings my attention is that this issue appears and disappears, once you fix it late on it goes back unfixed.” Ran a full, exhaustive hover-fill sweep of literally every actionable icon in the component before assuming anything: all 5 pinned rail buttons, the footer (Settings; Profile correctly excluded as permanently disabled), Panel actions/Collapse sidebar, all 11 overflow-menu “More” items (Gauge through Emailing — confirmed these already correctly fill via DropdownMenuItem's own built-in fillActionIcons/useActionIconFill wiring, which overrides the item's own explicit `filled={section.id === activeSectionId}` prop via React.cloneElement on hover — initially suspected as a bug at this call site, but confirmed correct after live testing, not just reading the code), and all 23 leaf/group items across both the Documents and Slides panel trees (Apps, Products, Food, Clothes, Sport and fitness, Office supplies, Kitchen, Outdoors, Garden, Auto, Orders, All orders, Returns, Order tracking, Sales, Gross margin, Expenses, Costs, Customers, Loyalty programs, Customer attrition, New customers, Customer satisfaction, plus Activity stream, Live operations, Participants, System logic, Rules engine, Triggers, Schedules, Daily, Monthly, Content). RESULT: only two failures, both the still-provisionally-exempted `video`/`videoSettings` icons from L-20 (“Activity stream”, “Live operations”) — everything else already filled correctly (confirming the L-24/L-25/L-26 fixes held). Re-evaluated L-20's premise directly: leaving two icons permanently un-fillable while every other actionable icon in the same component fills is not a neutral, defensible design choice — it is exactly the inconsistency the user is reporting as a bug, regardless of how visually different the real Fluent filled glyph looks. RESOLVED by restoring `filledD` on both entries in `FULL_PREVIEW_ICONS` (limbo-factory/src/data/rail-sidebar.ts), choosing L-20's option (a): accept the real Fluent filled variant as-is. IMPORTANT SELF-CAUGHT MISTAKE, worth recording so it isn't repeated: `video`'s filledD (already present in a code comment from L-20) was verified to match `node_modules/@fluentui/svg-icons/icons/video_20_filled.svg` byte-for-byte before use, but the first attempt at `videoSettings`'s filledD was WRONG — reconstructed from memory/reasoning about the icon's likely shape rather than read from the real file, producing a plausible-looking but fabricated path. Caught this before shipping by explicitly re-reading `node_modules/@fluentui/svg-icons/icons/video_settings_20_filled.svg` directly and comparing character-for-character; corrected to the real path before verifying live. This is a direct, concrete instance of the standing rule (Iconography protocol, and CLAUDE.md's checklist) that icon path data must always be sourced from the real Fluent `.svg` file, never approximated or reconstructed from reasoning about what an icon “probably” looks like — added as an explicit new checklist item (18) since this is exactly the kind of silent, plausible-looking error that would otherwise ship undetected. VERIFIED live in the browser after the fix: both icons now change their SVG `path d` attribute on hover, matching the real Fluent filled glyphs exactly (confirmed via direct string comparison against the two source .svg files again, post-fix). Re-ran the full sweep above a second time after the fix — zero failures across every icon in the sidebar (rail buttons, footer, overflow menu, both full panel trees), including explicit press (mousedown) and select (click-to-activate, stays-filled-after-mouse-leave) state checks, not just hover, per the user's explicit callout of all three states. `limbo-factory` typechecks cleanly after the change. Dispatched an independent code-review agent (icon-fill-audit-final) to verify this fix from a fresh, skeptical perspective and specifically investigate the user's “appears and disappears” observation — see that agent's findings for the root-cause hypothesis on session-to-session flakiness, folded into CLAUDE.md's Iconography protocol as a new mandatory safeguard once confirmed.
