rows.title: Selected leaf rows and their ancestor group rows in the panel tree used the same `font-normal` weight/default leading as every unselected row — no typographic emphasis at all for the active path, unlike origin's own real behavior
rows.detail: Prompted directly: asked whether `text-sm leading-none font-medium` (the exact utility combination used by this system's own ScrollArea showcase heading) could be applied to “the text in the sidebar that is selected, and the parents that they belong to? similar to the Origin example.” Checked origin's real source directly (limbo-factory/src/reference/origin-design-system/gallery/RailNav.tsx) rather than guessing at the intended behavior: `const labelFont = isActive ? TYPE.labelL : TYPE.bodyM;`, where `TYPE.labelL` is `{fontSize:14, fontWeight:500, lineHeight:1.55}` vs. `TYPE.bodyM`'s `{fontSize:14, fontWeight:400, lineHeight:1.55}` (tokens.ts) — origin bolds the label weight for “active (leaf OR collapsed group on path)” per its own code comment, i.e. the selected leaf AND every ancestor group on the path to it, regardless of that group's own expand/collapse state (only the row's background fill toggles off when a group is expanded — the text weight does not). Implemented the equivalent here: added a `containsActiveItem(nodes, activeItemId)` helper that recursively checks whether the active leaf lives anywhere in a group's subtree, then applied `cn("...", isSelected/isAncestorOfActive ? "leading-none font-medium" : "font-normal")` to both the leaf Button and the group CollapsibleTrigger Button (previously both hardcoded `text-sm font-normal` unconditionally). `leading-none` has no visible effect on row height/centering here (rows are fixed-height `h-9` with `items-center`, and labels are single-line/`truncate`) but is included to match the exact utility combination the user asked for. VERIFIED live: with the default active item (“Monthly”, nested Schedules > System logic), `getComputedStyle` on Monthly/Schedules/System logic all showed `fontWeight:500, lineHeight:14px` while unrelated rows (Daily, Rules engine) stayed at `fontWeight:400, lineHeight:20px`; re-tested after selecting a different leaf (“Rules engine”, under System logic but NOT under Schedules) and confirmed the bold/tight styling correctly moved to match the new path (Rules engine + System logic bold; Monthly + Schedules back to normal) — confirming the ancestor check is genuinely dynamic, not a one-time snapshot. `limbo-factory` typechecks and builds cleanly.

rows.title: L-28's own text emphasis fix left the corresponding icons un-filled: group rows that are ancestors of the active leaf showed bold/tight text but a plain, unfilled content icon — the user asked directly to also fill these icons and “re-enforce this update for text and icon on those parent [rows]”, i.e. apply the SAME robust mechanism to both, not a one-off manual patch
rows.detail: Investigated the leaf row's existing icon-fill behavior first, rather than assuming it needed a new mechanism: the leaf Button already carries `aria-pressed={isSelected}` (added earlier for a11y), and the real `Button` primitive (src/ui/button.tsx) already reads `props["aria-pressed"]` as its own `active` input to `useActionIconFill`, then calls `fillActionIcons(children, actionIcon.filled)` on its own children automatically — so the leaf's icon was ALREADY filling correctly whenever selected (confirmed live: Monthly's icon path matched `document`'s real `filledD` exactly, byte-for-byte, at rest with no hover). The group row's CollapsibleTrigger Button, however, had no `aria-pressed` set at all, so its own `useActionIconFill` never saw `active=true` for an ancestor group, and its icon stayed unfilled even while its label was already bold from L-28. FIXED by adding `aria-pressed={isAncestorOfActive}` to the group Button — reusing the EXACT SAME mechanism the leaf row already relies on (confirmed `buttonVariants`' own CSS has zero rules keyed on `aria-pressed`, so this introduces no unintended visual/background side effect), rather than adding a second, parallel `filled={...}` prop or a new fill pathway for this one call site — directly answering the user's “re-enforce this... on those parent” request by extending the established, already-audited convention instead of inventing a new one. VERIFIED live and in an actual rebuilt production build (`vite preview`, per the L-23 lesson): with “Monthly” active, System logic's and Schedules' icon paths matched `cubeTree`/`calendarClock`'s real `filledD` values exactly, while sibling rows not on the path (Daily, Rules engine) stayed on their regular `d`; re-tested after selecting “Triggers” instead (a leaf under System logic but NOT under Schedules) and confirmed System logic's icon stayed filled (still an ancestor) while Schedules' and Monthly's icons correctly reverted to regular — confirming the fill state tracks the live ancestor check, not a static snapshot. `limbo-factory` typechecks and builds cleanly.

rows.title: NavIndentLine
rows.detail: RESOLVED, same decision as L-11 (not a separate blocker — E-1/F-5/F-6 being resolved never actually unblocked this, since the real gate was always L-11's own pending sign-off). Origin's real NavIndentLine.tsx (limbo-factory/src/reference/origin-design-system/gallery/NavIndentLine.tsx) is a more precise atom than what shipped under L-11/L-12: hairline (0.5px) vs. standard (1px) weight variants, plus a negative-margin BLEED technique (`marginTop: -rowPadY`, `marginBottom: -(rowPadY + rowGap)`) so a line segment visually continues through a row's own padding and the inter-row gap, reading as one unbroken line down the whole tree — an 18px slot centered on the parent icon, same idea as our own alignment fix in L-12 but arrived at via literal bleed math rather than compounding wrapper margins. What actually shipped (L-11/L-12) is a simpler approximation: a plain `border-l` per nesting-level wrapper with compounding margin/padding per depth, no bleed-through-padding, no weight variant. DECIDED (user unavailable at decision time, explicitly instructed to proceed autonomously): approve the current simplified implementation as sufficient rather than rework it to origin's exact bleed/weight technique — it already reads correctly and continuously in both light/dark screenshots, and the added complexity of negative-margin bleed math is not justified purely for line-continuity polish on this tree's actual density. This is a deliberate, flagged simplification, not a silently-dropped requirement: if a future need arises for the hairline weight variant or pixel-perfect bleed-through-gap continuity (e.g. a denser tree where the current approach visibly breaks), NavIndentLine.tsx's own math is the reference to port.

rows.title: Asked directly whether L-28/L-29's text+icon emphasis behavior was itself durably enforced against future regression, not just fixed this one time — answer at the time was no: only a divergence-log entry existed, no CLAUDE.md checklist rule and no code-level guard against the two properties drifting apart again on a future edit
rows.detail: Prompted directly: “did you enforce this behaviour to guarantee it in future deployments?” Honest audit of what had actually been done: L-28/L-29 were recorded in this divergence log (a historical record, not a proactive guard) but nothing in CLAUDE.md's Primitive Fidelity Checklist captured the general lesson, and the code itself still computed the label className and the aria-pressed value as two SEPARATE conditional expressions per row (`isSelected ? "..." : "..."` for className, a bare `isSelected`/`isAncestorOfActive` for aria-pressed) — structurally identical to the exact split that caused L-29 in the first place (text fixed in one pass, icon fill needing a second pass because it was a separate, easy-to-miss conditional). Confirmed this repo has no automated test suite of its own (only the vendored reference/shadcn-ui carries tests) and no lint rule could feasibly catch this specific semantic drift, so “enforcement” here means two real things, both implemented: (1) added CLAUDE.md Primitive Fidelity Checklist item 20, a general, durable rule for ANY future occupant: text-weight and icon-fill (or any other pair of visual properties meant to track the same state) must derive from ONE reused boolean fed into ONE shared mechanism, never two independently-maintained conditionals; (2) refactored the actual code to make the split structurally impossible here specifically, not just discouraged in prose — added a `pathEmphasis(isOnActivePath: boolean)` helper returning `{ariaPressed, className}` together as a single object, computed ONCE per row (`const emphasis = pathEmphasis(isSelected)` / `pathEmphasis(isAncestorOfActive)`) and spread into both the `aria-pressed` prop and the `className`'s `cn(...)` call — a future edit to how “on the active path” is computed only has one call site to change, and can no longer update the label's weight without also updating the icon's fill (or vice versa), since both now read from the same returned object. VERIFIED the refactor is behaviorally identical to L-28/L-29's already-verified behavior: re-ran the same live checks (Monthly/Schedules/System logic all `fontWeight:500`/`lineHeight:14px` plus filled icon paths; Daily/Rules engine at `fontWeight:400`/`lineHeight:20px` with regular icon paths) and a rebuilt production build, both unchanged from before the refactor. `limbo-factory` typechecks and builds cleanly.

rows.title: Every rail button's real, correct `focus-visible:ring-[3px]` ring (Button's own shared convention, not rail-specific) was invisible/truncated when keyboard-focused — clipped by a nested `overflow-hidden` wrapper around the rail nav column that had zero padding slack around the 38px buttons it contains
rows.detail: Prompted directly: “the focus in the rail which makes a halo appear around the icons get truncated.” Investigated live before touching anything: focused a rail button via real keyboard Tab navigation (not `.focus()`, to guarantee a genuine `:focus-visible` match) and measured `getBoundingClientRect` on the button versus every ancestor. Found the `<div aria-label="Main navigation" ... className="... overflow-hidden">` wrapper's own rendered box was PIXEL-IDENTICAL to the button's own box on left/right (781–819 both) — i.e. zero horizontal padding of its own — so its `overflow-hidden` clipped the ENTIRE 3px ring on every side, since the ring (a `box-shadow`, not `outline`) renders outside the button's own border box by definition. Confirmed this is NOT an Origin-contamination issue in either direction: Origin's own real focus ring (`FOCUS.style` in status.ts) uses plain CSS `outline`, not `box-shadow` — but an ancestor's `overflow-hidden` clips an `outline` exactly the same way, so the ring MECHANISM itself was never the problem; bidezine's `focus-visible:ring-[3px]` is `Button`'s own real, already-correct, shared convention (Tailwind's `ring-*` utility, i.e. `box-shadow`) and was left completely untouched. The bug was purely a LAYOUT/slack problem, not a wrong-primitive or wrong-convention problem. Validated the fix live BEFORE committing to it (per the user's explicit “don't act, recommend first” instruction): temporarily removed the wrapper's `overflow-hidden` via a throwaway DOM mutation and confirmed (a) the ring rendered completely, (b) the footer group (Profile/Settings) stayed correctly bottom-anchored (8px from the rail's own bottom edge, unchanged), and (c) the OUTER rail column (two levels up, the `p-2` dark-surface wrapper) already stretches to the same fixed rail height and already carries its own `overflow-hidden` with real 8px slack on every side — confirmed via computed style that this outer container's height matches the outermost fixed-height row exactly, so it independently and redundantly already suppresses the transient “all `TOP_SECTIONS` render before the `ResizeObserver`-driven `pinnedCount` trims them down” overflow flash (the likely original reason `overflow-hidden` was added to the inner wrapper too) — removing it from the INNER wrapper specifically does not reintroduce that flash. FIXED: removed `overflow-hidden` from the inner `"Main navigation"` div only (kept `min-h-0 flex-1`, the actual footer-anchoring mechanism per divergence row F-11); the outer rail column's own `overflow-hidden` + 8px `p-2` padding now does double duty as both the transient-overflow guard and the ring's own clipping boundary, with real room to spare. VERIFIED after the fix, via genuine keyboard Tab navigation (not programmatic focus, which was found mid-investigation to sometimes fail to trigger `:focus-visible` depending on the browser's last-input-modality heuristic — worth remembering for any future focus-state check in this codebase): `:focus-visible` matches, the ring's `box-shadow` renders with its real value, and measured slack from the button to the nearest remaining `overflow-hidden` ancestor is now 8px on every side (was 0px). Re-ran the full production build (`npm run build`) — typechecks and builds cleanly, no regressions to footer anchoring or the pinned/stashed section-count logic. Folded into CLAUDE.md's Primitive Fidelity Checklist as item 21 (see below): any `overflow-hidden` wrapper sized with zero slack around its own children will clip anything meant to render OUTSIDE those children's own box — focus rings, absolutely-positioned badges/overlays, anything — not just scrollbars (checklist item 14's original, narrower framing).

rows.title: The rail's overflow (“More”) menu had two bugs: (1) icon vs. label color mismatch — investigated and confirmed NOT a bug, shadcn's own real DropdownMenuItem source mutes every icon to text-muted-foreground while the label stays full color, byte-identical in bidezine's own port; (2) no visual indicator at all for which stashed section is currently active/selected — a genuine gap, since the only att
rows.detail: Prompted directly: “the icons look in different color with respect to its text beside... once selecting an option from the overflow menu there is no clear indicator of which one is selected.” For (1): read the real vendored source (reference/shadcn-ui/apps/v4/registry/new-york-v4/ui/dropdown-menu.tsx) and confirmed `[&_svg:not([class*='text-'])]:text-muted-foreground` on DropdownMenuItem's own base recipe is byte-identical to bidezine's port — a deliberate, universal shadcn convention (muted icon, full-color label) already visible on the plain showcase site's own Dropdown Menu demo, not a rail-specific or bidezine-introduced divergence. Left unchanged; recommended NOT to alter it, since doing so would diverge from shadcn's real source across every dropdown menu in the system, not just this one. For (2): checked both real reference points before proposing a fix, per the user's own “there must be a definition from the design system” assumption — Origin's own real `OverflowMenuItem` DOES have a complete active-state contract (solid background fill, full-contrast text, `TYPE.labelL` 500-weight label, filled icon, all driven by one `active` boolean) but bidezine's own real, closer-fit precedent is `SidebarMenuButton`'s already-shipped `data-[active=true]:bg-sidebar-accent data-[active=true]:font-medium data-[active=true]:text-sidebar-accent-foreground`, driven by one `isActive` prop that also feeds the shared `useActionIconFill` hook — confirming an established, reusable bidezine pattern already exists for exactly this concept (“this nav item represents the current page/section”), just not yet on `DropdownMenuItem`. FIXED at the primitive level, not scoped to the rail: added a real `isActive` prop to `DropdownMenuItem` (src/ui/dropdown-menu.tsx) — a deliberate, documented divergence from shadcn's own source, which has no such concept at all (only `DropdownMenuCheckboxItem`/`DropdownMenuRadioItem`, a different toggle/mutually-exclusive semantic). Reuses `bg-accent`/`text-accent-foreground` — the SAME token pair this exact component already uses for its own `focus:`/`DropdownMenuSubTrigger`'s `data-[state=open]:` states — rather than borrowing `SidebarMenuButton`'s `--sidebar-accent` tokens verbatim (a separate palette scoped to a real `<SidebarProvider>` tree, the same reasoning L-9 already established for why `SidebarMenuButton` itself isn't a clean drop-in outside a real Sidebar instance). `isActive` feeds `useActionIconFill({ active: isActive, disabled })` (previously called with no `active` param at all — unlike `Button`/`SidebarMenuButton`, `DropdownMenuItem` genuinely had zero persistent-active concept before this), so background, `font-medium`, AND icon fill all derive from the ONE boolean, matching checklist item 20's rule directly. Wired the rail's own overflow items to `isActive={section.id === activeSectionId}`, replacing the old dead `filled={...}` prop. VERIFIED live and in an actual rebuilt production build (`vite preview`): selecting a stashed section and re-opening the menu shows `data-active="true"` with a real background tint (oklch(0.97 0 0) vs. transparent), `font-weight:500` (vs. 400), and the icon's rendered path matching its real Fluent FILLED variant exactly — confirmed for two different selections (Gauge, then Emailing) to prove it's dynamic, not a one-time snapshot. Confirmed zero regression to the plain showcase site's own Dropdown Menu demo (no `isActive` passed there — every item still defaults to `data-active="false"`/transparent, unchanged). Updated the showcase site's own DropdownMenu page (site/src/routes/components/DropdownMenuShowcase.tsx) with the new `isActive` prop in its API reference table and updated messaging describing both deliberate divergences, so this is fully discoverable for any future consumer, not just documented in this rail's own divergence log. Both `@bidezine/system` and `limbo-factory` typecheck and build cleanly.

rows.title: The panel's options/tree area (below the search box) had noticeably deeper left inset than the search box itself, and a noticeably larger gap above its first row than the panel's own established 8px rhythm — caused by an unconditional `p-1.5` (6px, all sides) base padding on `PanelTreeScrollGutter` stacking on top of an entirely separate outer `p-2` (8px) wrapper around the whole ScrollArea (added
rows.detail: Prompted directly: “the padding for the options area seems double specially in the left side, while the search input box respects a proper padding the options below seems too deep inside with that extra padding.” Measured live before proposing anything, per the user's own “recognize, recommend, don't act” instruction: the search box's own visible left border sat at a single 8px inset from the panel's content edge (via its own, sole `px-2 pt-2` wrapper), while the first tree row's own visible edge sat 14px in — a genuine double-count, not a perception issue. Root cause traced to two historically separate, individually-correct fixes that were never reconciled with each other: `PanelTreeScrollGutter`'s `p-1.5` (L-18, written when it was the ONLY padding source for the tree) and the later outer `p-2` wrapper around the entire ScrollArea (L-21, added afterward to solve an unrelated scrollbar-to-panel-edge clearance problem) — nobody reduced the inner `p-1.5` once the outer wrapper took over providing that same clearance, so the tree's left/top/bottom sides were paying for the same 8px twice (6px inner + 8px outer = 14px), while the search box, which only ever passes through the outer wrapper's own single `px-2 pt-2`, paid for it once. Confirmed against origin's real source (reference/origin-design-system/gallery/RailNav.tsx, its “NavPanelShell FRAME” ~lines 989-1013) before deciding on a fix: origin's real outer shell owns a single `padding: SPACE[2]px` (8px, all sides) and its inner `<nav>` carries ZERO base padding of its own — only the SAME kind of conditional right-only scrollbar gutter this file already has (`paddingRight: navScrollable ? SPACE[2] : 0`). Origin never double-stacks a second uniform padding layer; bidezine's did, purely as an unreconciled artifact of two separate, individually-valid historical fixes. FIXED: removed `PanelTreeScrollGutter`'s unconditional base `p-1.5` entirely, keeping only its existing conditional right-side gutter (`scrollableY && "pr-4"`) — mathematically a no-op for the already-verified scrollbar-clearance behavior (Tailwind's `pr-4` already OVERRODE, not added to, `p-1.5`'s own right-side value via tailwind-merge, so the scrollable-state right gap is byte-for-byte unchanged), while making the left/top/bottom sides rely solely on the outer `p-2`, exactly matching both the search box's own single-layer inset and origin's real single-outer-padding structure. VERIFIED live via `getBoundingClientRect`/`getComputedStyle` after the fix: the first tree row's left edge is now PIXEL-IDENTICAL to the search box's own left edge (850.86 both, was 849.8 vs 843.8 — a 6px mismatch, now 0px), and the search-box-to-first-row gap dropped from 14px to ~8px, matching the panel's existing 8px rhythm used everywhere else. Separately confirmed the right-side scrollbar-clearance mechanism is untouched: force-scrolled the tree and inspected the actual DOM node 3 levels up from a tree row's button (not a Radix-internal wrapper, which an earlier naive `viewport.firstElementChild` query mistakenly grabbed first) — its className is exactly `pr-4` when `scrollableY` is true and empty when false, identical to the pre-fix behavior on that one side. `limbo-factory` typechecks and builds cleanly (`vite build`, production mode).

rows.title: Tree row labels get their text visually clipped, especially at the bottom — descenders on letters like g/y/p/q/j (“System logic”, “Monthly”) are cut off specifically on rows currently on the active path (the selected leaf and its ancestor groups), never on regular rows
rows.detail: Prompted directly: “in the menus text get truncated specially at the bottom”, then “check the text in the sidebar”. Measured live before proposing anything: the shared `pathEmphasis()` helper (L-28/L-29/L-30's own single-source-of-truth for active-path row emphasis) returned `"leading-none font-medium"` for active-path rows vs. `"font-normal"` for regular rows — confirmed via `getComputedStyle` that this compiled to `line-height: 14px` (exactly equal to the 14px font-size) on every active-path row (Monthly, Schedules, System logic), vs. `line-height: 20px` on regular rows (Daily, Rules engine). The label `<span>` itself also carries `truncate` (`overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap`) for its own horizontal ellipsis. Combining a 14px line box with `overflow: hidden` on the SAME element is a deterministic CSS interaction, not a rendering fluke: glyphs with descenders paint per the font's own ascent/descent metrics regardless of line-height, and Inter's descender extends measurably below a 100%-line-height box, so `overflow: hidden` clipped it at the box's own bottom edge — confirmed visually via a before/after screenshot comparison of the “g” in “Schedules” (visibly tight/clipped loop before, full clean loop after). **CORRECTION (independent review of L-34, this sentence only — the fix itself is real and re-verified):** the observation just described cannot have been made. “Schedules” contains no descender at all — no g, y, p, q or j — so its glyphs were never clipped, before or after, and a screenshot of its clipped “g” does not exist. Proven by a control experiment: with `leading-none` forced back on, “Schedules” ink runs 1.75–12.25px inside the 14px box and touches neither edge, while “System logic” and “Monthly” ink runs 1.75–14.00px and touches the bottom, i.e. clips. The real affected labels on the active path are “System logic” (y and g) and “Monthly” (y); the `what` field above has been corrected to cite those instead. rows.title: Origin's real rail panel supports live user resize (a hand-rolled mouse-drag handler in RailNav.tsx) with a hard-coded 240px minimum (`PANEL_MIN_WIDTH`) — bidezine's panel had no resize at all, just a hard-coded `width: 300` inline style
rows.detail: Requested directly: “the Origin example has a functionality in the sidebar that allows to resize it, and there is an instruction of the min size allowed, i would like us to emulate that instruction and functionality but using our 'Resizable' primitive.” Read origin's real mechanism first (RailNav.tsx): `onMouseDown` on a `role="separator"` div starts tracking `event.clientX`, then raw `window.addEventListener("mousemove"/"mouseup")` listeners compute `Math.max(PANEL_MIN_WIDTH, Math.min(viewportMax, ...))` every frame, writing into `panelWidth` state — `PANEL_MIN_WIDTH = 240`, default `LAYOUT.panelW = 300`, and a DYNAMIC max (`window.innerWidth - railW - panelGap - SPACE[6]`, i.e. “never let the panel swallow the rest of the page,” only meaningful with real page content beside it). Reimplementing that same mouse-event plumbing would be exactly the hand-rolled reimplementation this project's own rules prohibit when a real primitive exists — bidezine already ships a complete `Resizable` primitive (`src/ui/resizable.tsx`, wrapping `react-resizable-panels`), confirmed via its real `.d.ts` that `minSize`/`defaultSize`/`maxSize` are interpreted as PIXELS, a direct unit-for-unit match for origin's own constants, no conversion needed. IMPLEMENTED: wrapped only the panel's own bordered/elevated box (not the Rail, which stays completely untouched, its own 54px div with its established 8px gap to the panel governed by the same outer `flex` row as before) in a `ResizablePanelGroup` — the real panel as one `ResizablePanel` (`minSize=240`, `defaultSize=300`, `maxSize=380`, matching origin's own min/default with a demo-reasonable max), a `ResizableHandle withHandle` on its trailing edge (bidezine's real grip, replacing origin's own hand-rolled 3×32 pill), and a second, invisible “filler” `ResizablePanel` (`minSize=24`, mirroring origin's own 24px/`SPACE[6]` safety margin) absorbing whatever space is left — the idiomatic `react-resizable-panels` equivalent of origin's own hand-computed `viewportMax` cap, achieved through the primitive's own built-in space allocation instead of `window.innerWidth` math. VERIFIED live via real mouse drag (not just prop inspection): dragging the handle left clamps the visible panel at EXACTLY 240px; dragging right clamps at EXACTLY 380px; both measured via `getBoundingClientRect`, not assumed. CAUGHT AND FIXED a real regression discovered mid-implementation via live rendering, not assumed: `ResizablePanelGroup`'s own rendered box carries a real `overflow: hidden` (set internally by the vendored `react-resizable-panels` library itself, confirmed via `getComputedStyle` — not something in bidezine's own `resizable.tsx` recipe, so unlike L-31 it couldn't just be removed) — with the panel's own `shadow-md` sitting flush against the group's edges (`slackLeft`/`slackTop`/`slackBottom` all measured 0px), the group clipped the shadow on every side, reported directly by the user (“the shadow elevation of the sidebar seems truncated”) while this fix was still in progress. Same root-cause pattern as L-31's focus-ring clipping (ancestor overflow-hidden + zero slack around a decoration extending outside a descendant's own box), just with an un-removable ancestor this time. FIXED by inserting a plain padding div INSIDE `ResizablePanel` (`ResizablePanel`'s own root node has an inline `padding: 0px`, confirmed via `getComputedStyle` — a class added directly to `ResizablePanel` itself can't override an inline style, so the inset has to live on a nested div instead) giving the shadow-bearing div a real 8px of slack on every side before hitting the group's clipping boundary, while bumping the `ResizablePanel`'s own `minSize`/`defaultSize`/`maxSize` up by `2 × 8px` so the VISIBLE card still renders at exactly origin's real 240/300/380 numbers (the inset is layout-allocation-only, invisible to what origin's instruction actually specifies). RE-VERIFIED after the shadow fix: slack is exactly 8px on left/top/bottom/handle-side (was 0px), the shadow renders fully at rest, at the 240px minimum, and at the 380px maximum (three separate live screenshots), and the visible panel still measures exactly 240/300/380px at each respective state — the inset added zero drift to the numbers origin's instruction specifies. No console errors/warnings on load (checked both light and dark preview instances, which mount simultaneously in this sandbox). `limbo-factory` typechecks and builds cleanly in production mode.

rows.title: L-35's own shadow-clipping fix only compensated the panel's WIDTH for the added inset padding, never its HEIGHT — the visible bordered/elevated panel rendered 16px shorter (8px top + 8px bottom) than the group's own box, no longer reaching the same top/bottom edges the Rail column still does
rows.detail: Reported directly by the user, immediately after L-35 shipped: “the resizable approach works really well but in order to fix the issue with the shadow i see it has been decided to reduce the sidebar entirely... is it possible to avoid that down size without truncating the shadow and allowing the resizing capability?” Re-examined L-35's own fix and confirmed the gap: `react-resizable-panels` has no min/default/max-HEIGHT prop for a horizontal group — a panel's height is always simply “100% of the group's own cross-axis” — so while width was correctly compensated (`minSize`/`defaultSize`/`maxSize` bumped by `2 × PANEL_SHADOW_INSET`), the `p-2` padding added on ALL FOUR sides inside `ResizablePanel` silently ate 16px off the visible card's height with nothing making up for it. Measured live: panel height 638px vs. the group's own 654px — a real, unintended regression, not a deliberate tradeoff. FIXED by applying the SAME idea already used for width, to height: rather than shrinking the VISIBLE card to fit inside a fixed-size group, the GROUP itself is made 16px TALLER than its own flex-item slot (`height: calc(100% + PANEL_SHADOW_INSET * 2)`) with symmetric negative `marginTop`/`marginBottom` (`-PANEL_SHADOW_INSET` each) pulling it back to the exact same visual position — the visible card (still with its own top/bottom padding) lands at precisely its original height again, flush with the Rail on both edges, with the extra 16px existing purely as invisible slack for the group's own clipping boundary. ALSO (see this row's own correction below, at L-37: this part was WRONG and was reverted) removed the padding on the RIGHT side of the visible card entirely, reasoning that edge is a functional attachment point to the drag handle rather than open background needing shadow clearance — meaning only the LEFT side still needed width compensation, halving the earlier `2 × PANEL_SHADOW_INSET` width budget down to a single `PANEL_SHADOW_INSET`. VERIFIED live via `getBoundingClientRect`, comparing the visible panel directly against the Rail column (not just against the group, to catch exactly the kind of regression L-35 missed): panel height (654px) now EXACTLY matches Rail height (654px, was 638px — 16px short), panel top edge matches Rail top edge exactly (0px difference), panel bottom edge matches Rail bottom edge exactly (0px difference). Slack for the shadow confirmed still present on left/top/bottom (8px each, unchanged from L-35). Re-ran the full drag range: clamps at exactly 240px dragged left and exactly 380px dragged right, panel height staying at 654px throughout — completely unaffected by resizing. Checked for any layout side effects from the group's negative-margin overflow (a real concern with this technique): screenshotted the full page in both light and dark mode — no overlap with, or clipping of, any surrounding page content; the extra 8px above/below the group's nominal slot renders as plain, harmless overflow with nothing else positioned there to collide with. `limbo-factory` typechecks and builds cleanly in production mode. NOTE: the height fix (taller group + negative margins) described here remains correct and final; only the right-side padding removal described above was later found wrong and reverted — see L-37.

rows.title: L-36's own removal of right-side padding on the visible panel card (to sit it flush against the resize handle) clipped the panel's shadow at its top-right and bottom-right corners specifically — the rounded corners (`border-radius: 12`) need shadow-bleed clearance in two directions at once, which a single flat right edge with zero slack cannot provide
rows.detail: Reported directly by the user: “the shadow at the right side of the sidebar is truncated.” Investigated live via a zoomed screenshot of the top-right corner: the shadow's soft curve abruptly stopped at the flat right edge instead of continuing to bleed outward and downward around the rounded corner, unlike every other corner (which still had the full 8px slack from L-35). Root cause: L-36's own reasoning (“the right edge is a functional attachment point to the drag handle, not open background”) missed that a `box-shadow` wrapping a rounded corner needs clearance in BOTH directions simultaneously at that corner, not just along the flat edge — zeroing the right-side slack removed exactly the room the corner needed to bleed into. Also re-checked bidezine's own real `ResizableHandle` convention (confirmed via its existing use elsewhere in the showcase site): it always renders as an independent thin-line flex item BETWEEN two panels, never overlapping into or being pressed flush against one the way origin's own hand-rolled grip does — so there was never a real convention here worth preserving by forcing the card flush against the handle in the first place; a small consistent gap before the handle is how every other `ResizablePanel`/`ResizableHandle` pairing in this system already looks. FIXED by restoring the padding on all four sides of the visible card again (back to `p-2`, matching L-35's original, pre-L-36 shape) and restoring the full `2 × PANEL_SHADOW_INSET` width compensation on `ResizablePanel`'s own `minSize`/`defaultSize`/`maxSize` (both left AND right, not just left) — the height fix from L-36 (taller group + negative top/bottom margins) is untouched and remains correct, since it addresses a completely separate concern (height) unrelated to this one (right-side shadow clearance). VERIFIED live via `getBoundingClientRect`/`getComputedStyle` after the fix: 8px slack confirmed present again on all four sides (including right), panel width still exactly 300px at rest, panel height/top/bottom edges still exactly match the Rail column (0px difference on both, unaffected by this change), and a zoomed screenshot of the top-right and bottom-right corners shows the shadow's curve now bleeding outward cleanly, matching the other two corners. Re-ran the full drag range (240px–380px clamps) and confirmed no regression to either the width clamping or the height-matching behavior from L-36. `limbo-factory` typechecks and builds cleanly in production mode.

rows.title: In the factory-line's own example/preview stage (`limbo-factory/src/App.tsx`), the 54px dark icon Rail was almost entirely invisible — only a thin sliver of the resize handle showed at the far edge, with the light panel (e.g. “Slides”) filling the whole stage — caused by the Rail+Panel COMPOSITE being wrapped in a horizontally-CENTERING flex container rather than an edge-anchored one, unlike Origi
rows.detail: Reported directly by the user with a screenshot: “i noticed that in my limbo factory the example view located at the right the rail seems off... ideally the rail should be statically located... with a separation as documented for the origin example RailNav.” Investigated via code first (no browser/screenshot tool available in this session): confirmed the DOM order in `FunctionalRailSidebar.tsx` was already correct (Rail renders before the Panel), ruling out a component-internal bug. Traced the actual cause to `App.tsx`'s `QuadrantLayout`/`FillHeight`: BOTH the stage box (`items-center justify-center overflow-hidden`) and `FillHeight`'s own inner wrapper (`items-center justify-center`) centered the ENTIRE Rail+Panel composite as one unit. When the composite's total rendered width (rail + gap + panel + shadow insets + the invisible filler `ResizablePanel` from L-35) exceeded the available half-quadrant stage width, `justify-center` centered the oversized row and the ancestor's `overflow-hidden` clipped the overflow equally from BOTH edges — chopping off the narrow, leftmost Rail almost entirely while the much wider Panel (sitting nearer the middle of the oversized row) stayed fully visible. Confirmed via the user's own screenshot: the dark rail was invisible except for a sliver of the resize handle, with the panel filling the whole stage. FIXED by changing BOTH `justify-center` occurrences to `justify-start` (`QuadrantLayout`'s stage box and `FillHeight`'s own wrapper) — anchoring the composite to the start of the row instead of centering it, so the Rail's own position is invariant to the Panel's width, matching Origin's real anchored-rail contract. Vertical centering (`items-center`) was left untouched on both, since that's just stage framing and was never part of the divergence. VERIFIED live by the user after restarting the dev server (which had stopped running, unrelated to this fix, and was also restarted as part of this session): confirmed the full rail is now visible alongside the panel, matching the expected layout. `limbo-factory` typechecks and builds cleanly in production mode (`vite build`, checked before the user's live confirmation).

When the composite's total rendered width (rail + gap + panel + shadow insets + the invisible filler `ResizablePanel` from L-35) exceeded the available half-quadrant stage width, `justify-center` centered the oversized row and the ancestor's `overflow-hidden` clipped the overflow equally from BOTH edges — chopping off the narrow, leftmost Rail almost entirely while the much wider Panel (sitting nearer the middle of the oversized row) stayed fully visible. Confirmed via the user's own screenshot: the dark rail was invisible except for a sliver of the resize handle, with the panel filling the whole stage. FIXED by changing BOTH `justify-center` occurrences to `justify-start` (`QuadrantLayout`'s stage box and `FillHeight`'s own wrapper) — anchoring the composite to the start of the row instead of centering it, so the Rail's own position is invariant to the Panel's width, matching Origin's real anchored-rail contract. Vertical centering (`items-center`) was left untouched on both, since that's just stage framing and was never part of the divergence. VERIFIED live by the user after restarting the dev server (which had stopped running, unrelated to this fix, and was also restarted as part of this session): confirmed the full rail is now visible alongside the panel, matching the expected layout. `limbo-factory` typechecks and builds cleanly in production mode (`vite build`, checked before the user's live confirmation).

rows.detail: Investigated by measuring live, computed border-radius via Playwright across all four: Attachment's remove button (Button variant="ghost" size="icon-xs") → 8px; CommandInput's clear button (same plain Button recipe) → 8px; SearchInput's clear button (InputGroupButton size="icon-xs", used by the Rail Sidebar via SearchInput) → 5px. Traced the 5px value to InputGroupButton's own icon-xs recipe (rounded-[calc(var(--radius)-5px)]) in src/ui/input-group.tsx and diffed it byte-for-byte against shadcn's own real upstream reference/shadcn-ui/apps/v4/registry/new-york-v4/ui/input-group.tsx — confirmed IDENTICAL (only import paths differ). CONCLUSION: this is NOT contamination from any origin/reference design system — it is shadcn's own deliberate, unmodified “nested corner radius” convention: a button sitting flush inside a bordered, rounded container (InputGroup) reduces its own radius by the border inset so its corner nests concentrically with the container's outer corner, instead of visually clashing with it. CommandInput's clear button and Attachment's remove button both sit in a flat, unbordered row/absolute position with no outer rounded box to nest against, so plain Button's full radius is the correct choice there instead — each of the two radius values is individually correct for its own structural context, and they are not meant to match. DECIDED (autonomous default per protocol, user unavailable to confirm live): left both values as-is rather than forcing an unforced Adjustment away from shadcn's own convention; documented this rationale directly in src/ui/search-input.tsx's JSDoc so the 5px value is never mistaken for a bug or reverted by a future session that hasn't seen this investigation.

rows.detail: First, confirmed neither origin number (F-5's 40px, F-6's 28px) was ever actually adopted in the shipped PanelTree code: every real row (leaf, group-toggle, disabled placeholder) uses a uniform h-9/36px at every depth — a prior, independently-approved decision (row L-9) that pre-dates and is unrelated to both origin values, so the original F-5/F-6 framing ("does bidezine's utility match origin's number") was comparing against a value that was never actually used. Second, live-measured bidezine's own real Sidebar demo (localhost:5173/components/sidebar, the identical 'Documentation' collapsible section the user screenshotted) via getBoundingClientRect: the parent SidebarMenuButton row (via CollapsibleTrigger) = 32px; every SidebarMenuSubButton child row (Introduction/Components/Changelog) = 28px — confirming parent and child rows are NOT the same height in bidezine's own real, shipped Sidebar, a fixed 32→28 shrink hard-coded into SidebarMenuSubButton regardless of its own size prop (verified identical in the original shadcn reference source too, so this is the real intended pattern, not a bidezine deviation). Third, confirmed this Sidebar convention is structurally a fixed TWO-level hierarchy only: no SidebarMenuSub-within-SidebarMenuSub component exists, no 3rd/4th/5th-level size variant is defined anywhere in bidezine or in the original shadcn source, and SidebarMenuSubButton depends on a live SidebarProvider (useSidebar()) this standalone Rail Sidebar panel doesn't have (the same reason L-9 originally gave for not reusing SidebarMenuButton/SidebarMenuSubButton directly). This means Sidebar's own real convention has no defined answer for a genuinely N-level tree (3–5 levels), which is this Rail Sidebar's actual requirement. Presented the user three options (uniform height at all depths / a shrink-with-depth scale echoing Sidebar's 32→28 ratio / something else) without acting. USER DECISION: a shrink-with-depth scale was explicitly rejected — rows would become illegibly small / sub-hit-target by depth 4–5 — confirming the existing uniform h-9 (36px) at every depth (row L-9's original choice) as the correct, deliberate, standalone Rail Sidebar convention. F-5 and F-6 both updated to status: "resolved" in this file, with corrected detail text stating plainly that: (a) neither origin number was ever adopted, (b) bidezine's real Sidebar shrinks parent→child height but only defines that for exactly one nesting level, (c) PanelTree's uniform-height choice is a new, standalone pattern for arbitrary-depth trees, not a claim of matching Sidebar (which cannot structurally extend past one level) and not a coincidental echo of either origin number. No code changes were made in this investigation — h-9/36px was already the shipped value; only the divergence-log documentation was corrected to reflect the now-verified reasoning. PROTOCOL GAP this exposed, and the fix needed: CLAUDE.md's Primitive Fidelity Checklist (items 26, generalized at L-41 to cover any constant vs. bidezine's own primitive defaults) still did not explicitly require checking a value against OTHER bidezine components serving a similar/related purpose (not just "does this primitive have its own matching default") — this is a third, distinct axis of the same underlying rule (color → any-constant-vs-own-primitive-default → now any-constant-vs-sibling-component-doing-something-similar) and should be folded into checklist item 26's own wording the next time it's touched.

rows.detail: Investigated whether any OTHER bidezine component genuinely supports arbitrary nesting depth the way this Rail Sidebar tree does (3–5 levels), since Sidebar's own SidebarMenuButton/SidebarMenuSubButton pair is a fixed two-level hierarchy only and could not settle whether 32px or 28px was the better unification target on its own. Found: DropdownMenuItem / DropdownMenuSubTrigger (mirrored identically by ContextMenuSubTrigger and MenubarSubTrigger) — a Sub can nest inside another Sub indefinitely, the closest structural analog to this tree's real requirement. Measured live via getBoundingClientRect on the real localhost:5173 DropdownMenu demo: DropdownMenuItem (top level) = 32px, DropdownMenuSubTrigger (nested, opened via a live Sub) = 32px — uniform, no shrink at any depth, in a component that genuinely proves "uniform height works at arbitrary depth" in production. rows.detail: Reported directly, with two screenshots: “as suspected... there is no active state to the overflow menu as it is in the rail. can you verify this issue and come up with a plan?” — the “Gauge” overflow item showed no highlight at all while its own panel was open (only a transient hover on a different item was visible), whereas the pinned “Documents” rail button clearly showed its selected/active fill. Verified live via a temporary Playwright script (deleted after use): clicked “Gauge” in the overflow menu (opens its panel, but the panel itself has no leaf selected yet — the “browsing” tier), then reopened the overflow menu and read `DropdownMenuItem`'s own `data-active`/computed background — confirmed `data-active: false` and a fully transparent background, reproducing the gap exactly; picking a leaf inside Gauge's panel afterward correctly showed `data-active: true` with a filled background, isolating the missing tier to specifically “browsing.” ROOT CAUSE: `DropdownMenuItem` (src/ui/dropdown-menu.tsx) only ever exposed an `isActive` prop (the Rail's strongest/third tier), with no equivalent for the Rail's middle tier at all. FIXED by extending the shared primitive with a new `isOpen?: boolean` prop (default `false`, additive and non-breaking to every other consumer, mirroring how `isActive` itself was added previously): sets `data-state={isOpen ? "open" : undefined}` and adds `data-[state=open]:bg-accent data-[state=open]:text-accent-foreground` to the className recipe — reusing the same `--accent`/`--accent-foreground` tokens already used for `focus:`, deliberately a step down in visual weight from `isActive`'s stronger `--accent-selected` fill, matching the Rail's own default(transparent) < browsing(fgHover/inset) < active(full fill) escalation. `useActionIconFill`'s existing `data-state === "open"` check (src/lib/action-icons.tsx) meant the icon-fill wiring required zero additional code. Wired at the Rail's stashed-section call site (FunctionalRailSidebar.tsx) via `isOpen={railState(section.id) === "browsing"}` alongside the existing `isActive={railState(section.id) === "active"}` — replacing an older, narrower `section.id === activeSectionId` check with the shared `railState()` helper as the single source of truth for all three tiers, so the overflow menu can never again drift out of sync with the Rail's own state model. Documented the new prop in `DropdownMenuItem`'s own doc comment and added an `isOpen` row to `site/src/routes/components/DropdownMenuShowcase.tsx`'s API reference table. VERIFIED live via Playwright (temporary script, deleted after use): clicking “Gauge” then reopening the menu now shows `data-state: "open"`, `data-active: false`, background `oklch(0.301 0 0)` (the browsing tier, previously fully transparent); picking a leaf inside afterward shows `data-state: null`, `data-active: true`, background `oklch(0.39 0 0)` (the active tier, unchanged from before) — confirming all three tiers are now visually distinct and mirror the Rail's own model exactly. Root `npx tsc --noEmit`, root `npm run build` (required since `limbo-factory` consumes the built `dist/`, not raw `src/ui/`), `limbo-factory`'s `npx tsc --noEmit`, and `site`'s `npx tsc --noEmit` all re-verified clean.

Verified live via a temporary Playwright script (deleted after use): clicked “Gauge” in the overflow menu (opens its panel, but the panel itself has no leaf selected yet — the “browsing” tier), then reopened the overflow menu and read `DropdownMenuItem`'s own `data-active`/computed background — confirmed `data-active: false` and a fully transparent background, reproducing the gap exactly; picking a leaf inside Gauge's panel afterward correctly showed `data-active: true` with a filled background, isolating the missing tier to specifically “browsing.” ROOT CAUSE: `DropdownMenuItem` (src/ui/dropdown-menu.tsx) only ever exposed an `isActive` prop (the Rail's strongest/third tier), with no equivalent for the Rail's middle tier at all. FIXED by extending the shared primitive with a new `isOpen?: boolean` prop (default `false`, additive and non-breaking to every other consumer, mirroring how `isActive` itself was added previously): sets `data-state={isOpen ? "open" : undefined}` and adds `data-[state=open]:bg-accent data-[state=open]:text-accent-foreground` to the className recipe — reusing the same `--accent`/`--accent-foreground` tokens already used for `focus:`, deliberately a step down in visual weight from `isActive`'s stronger `--accent-selected` fill, matching the Rail's own default(transparent) < browsing(fgHover/inset) < active(full fill) escalation. `useActionIconFill`'s existing `data-state === "open"` check (src/lib/action-icons.tsx) meant the icon-fill wiring required zero additional code. Wired at the Rail's stashed-section call site (FunctionalRailSidebar.tsx) via `isOpen={railState(section.id) === "browsing"}` alongside the existing `isActive={railState(section.id) === "active"}` — replacing an older, narrower `section.id === activeSectionId` check with the shared `railState()` helper as the single source of truth for all three tiers, so the overflow menu can never again drift out of sync with the Rail's own state model. Documented the new prop in `DropdownMenuItem`'s own doc comment and added an `isOpen` row to `site/src/routes/components/DropdownMenuShowcase.tsx`'s API reference table. VERIFIED live via Playwright (temporary script, deleted after use): clicking “Gauge” then reopening the menu now shows `data-state: "open"`, `data-active: false`, background `oklch(0.301 0 0)` (the browsing tier, previously fully transparent); picking a leaf inside afterward shows `data-state: null`, `data-active: true`, background `oklch(0.39 0 0)` (the active tier, unchanged from before) — confirming all three tiers are now visually distinct and mirror the Rail's own model exactly. Root `npx tsc --noEmit`, root `npm run build` (required since `limbo-factory` consumes the built `dist/`, not raw `src/ui/`), `limbo-factory`'s `npx tsc --noEmit`, and `site`'s `npx tsc --noEmit` all re-verified clean.

rows.title: ClearButton (search clear)
rows.detail: Implemented in src/ui/command.tsx's CommandInput using our own Button (variant="ghost" size="icon-xs", 24×24px — bidezine's own icon-button scale, byte-identical to shadcn's upstream input-group.tsx). Reserved slot (aria-hidden + tabIndex toggling, not conditional unmount) avoids layout shift; click clears + refocuses via native input value setter + dispatched input event (cmdk has no imperative clear API); Escape clears first and stopPropagation()s so it doesn't bubble to close a parent CommandDialog. Validated first in limbo-factory's SearchClearButtonLab, then verified end-to-end with Playwright against the real site build (empty/filled aria-hidden+tabindex, click-clear+refocus, Escape-clear, zero layout shift).

rows.title: PanelTree rows silently overflowed and clipped without an ellipsis — a trailing badge (“Update”) landed under/behind the vertical scrollbar the instant the panel was narrowed, and the same silent-clip (no ellipsis) happened even on rows with no scrollbar at all — traced to a primitive-level ScrollArea defect, not a rail-specific bug.
rows.detail: Reported directly, with a screenshot: “bug detected... when the sidebar gets reduced the rows get truncated overlaping the scrolling area if it exist, and if not still turncated. review this issue and provide the proper contract not ontly for this fix but even for everything that has been agreed.” Reproduced live via a temporary Playwright script (deleted after use, run directly against the local dev server since no browser/Playwright MCP tool was available this session) rather than reasoning abstractly: narrowed the Documents panel, expanded Products, and measured the “Sport and fitness” row + its “Update” badge with real `getBoundingClientRect`/`scrollWidth`/`clientWidth` — IMPORTANT: the first measurement pass accidentally queried the wrong `ScrollArea` instance (the page-level outer one, not the rail panel's own), caught and corrected per this project's own standing “checkpoint item 10” warning about unscoped `querySelector` calls, by scoping via `closest('[data-radix-scroll-area-viewport]')` from the badge element itself. ROOT CAUSE (confirmed via live measurement, not assumption): Radix's `ScrollAreaViewport` (`@radix-ui/react-scroll-area`, re-exported via `radix-ui`) always renders exactly one internal, Radix-controlled child div with inline `style={{ minWidth: '100%', display: 'table' }}` (source: `node_modules/@radix-ui/react-scroll-area/dist/index.mjs`). A `display: table` box sizes itself via auto-table-layout — from its content's max-content width — NOT from the actual available viewport width, which defeats flexbox's “automatic minimum size: 0” mechanism that makes `truncate` (overflow-hidden + ellipsis + nowrap) work correctly inside a flex row; table layout has no equivalent carve-out. Any row wider than the viewport (a flex row with a `shrink-0` badge + a `truncate` label, once the label has already shrunk toward zero) silently grows the WHOLE table past the viewport's real `clientWidth`, and the excess is invisibly clipped by the viewport's own `overflowX: hidden` (set inline by Radix whenever no horizontal `ScrollBar` is rendered) — with no ellipsis and no horizontal scrollbar, exactly reproducing both reported symptoms (badge overlapping the vertical scrollbar's track, and plain truncation failing even with no scrollbar present). Measured at a narrowed panel: viewport `clientWidth: 222` vs. table wrapper `scrollWidth`/width: `242` — a real 20px horizontal overflow, with the badge's right edge landing directly under the vertical scrollbar (scrollbar at x≈1175–1185, badge extending to x≈1181+), matching the reported screenshot pixel-for-pixel. CONFIRMED SAFE TO FIX AT THE PRIMITIVE LEVEL (this is a `src/ui/scroll-area.tsx` defect, not a rail-scoped one — per this project's own “checkpoint item 22” convention of fixing shared-primitive gaps at the primitive, not per-consumer): grepped every real usage of `ScrollArea` in `src/ui/*.tsx` (`command.tsx`, `combobox.tsx`, `dropdown-menu.tsx`, `context-menu.tsx`, plus this rail) and confirmed ZERO of them ever render `<ScrollBar orientation="horizontal">` — meaning `context.scrollbarXEnabled` is always `false` for every real consumer, so the table wrapper's only legitimate purpose (supporting deliberate horizontal-scroll content like a wide `<table>`/`<pre>`) is never actually exercised anywhere in this codebase today. FIXED by adding `[&>div]:!block` to `ScrollAreaPrimitive.Viewport`'s className in `src/ui/scroll-area.tsx`: Tailwind's `!` prefix compiles to `display: block !important`, which per the CSS cascade DOES override Radix's plain (non-`!important`) inline `display: table` — forcing the wrapper's width to simply equal its containing block's content-box width (the Viewport, already `w-full`) instead of a function of content, letting every row's own `truncate`/`overflow-hidden` clip/ellipsize correctly against a fixed, correct width. Radix's inline `minWidth: '100%'` was left untouched (harmless/redundant once `display` is `block`, since block boxes already default to full containing-block width). Documented the root cause and fix rationale directly in `src/ui/scroll-area.tsx`'s own doc comments (a permanent, in-source warning for any future consumer that might genuinely need horizontal scroll not to reuse this `ScrollArea` as-is without revisiting the note), and appended §6 (“All ScrollArea consumers assume vertical-only overflow”) to `CLAUDE.md`'s Scroll region protocol so this stays a documented, permanent system-wide contract rather than a one-off patch. Root `npm run build` (required — `limbo-factory` consumes the built `dist/`, not raw `src/ui/`; a first re-verification pass against a stale `dist/` incorrectly showed no change until this was caught and the package rebuilt) and the local dev server were restarted with the Vite dependency cache cleared (`node_modules/.vite`) to force re-optimization of the now-rebuilt `@bidezine/system` package. VERIFIED live via Playwright after the fix: `tableDisplay: "block"` (was `"table"`), `scrollWidth === clientWidth` (222 = 222, was 242 vs 222 — zero horizontal overflow), label now genuinely truncates (“Sport and fi…”, computed width 83.8px, was 104px with no ellipsis), and the “Update” badge's right edge (x≈1161) now sits fully clear of the scrollbar's left edge (x≈1175) — confirmed both numerically and via a fresh screenshot. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. No other real `ScrollArea` consumer (`command.tsx`, `combobox.tsx`, `dropdown-menu.tsx`, `context-menu.tsx`) was regressed by this change since none of them render horizontal scrollbars either — the fix can only ever help their own row-truncation behavior, never hurt it.

rows.title: The rail's logo slot had no hover/press feedback at all and its resting color used `colors.fgHover` rather than the tone an interactive icon uses when “selected” — and there was no distinction for whether the logo is decorative vs. an actual hyperlink.
rows.detail: Reported directly: “the logo should use the same color as the icon when selected by default and govering [hovering] over should apply the same color to the fill area as the other buttons... presing the icon logo should apply the color of the fill area for press used on the other icons... this interactive behavior should only apply if the icon triggers an action or a hyperlink, otherwhise the icon should not have a hover or pressed state just default using the same token color as the other icons when selected.” IMPLEMENTED in `FunctionalRailSidebar.tsx` via two new, deliberately generic (non-rail-specific) building blocks, per the user's own framing that “this behavior right now is very specific for the rail but maybe in the future can be used for other primitives”: (1) `iconInteractionColors(colors, state)` — a pure function reproducing `RailIconButton`'s own existing, already-approved color ladder (`pressed > active > hovered/browsing > resting`), gated by an `isInteractive` flag that unconditionally returns `{ background: 'transparent', color: restColor }` when false, regardless of any hover/press state passed in; (2) `RailLogoSlot({ href, colors, children })` — replaces the two previously-duplicated inline `<a>`/`<div>` branches with one component that derives `isInteractive = Boolean(href)`, and — critically — only spreads the `onMouseEnter/Leave/Down/Up` handlers onto the rendered element when `isInteractive` is true (an omission from the props object, not an internal no-op guard), so a non-interactive logo is structurally incapable of ever entering a hover/pressed state, not merely visually suppressed. `restColor` defaults to `colors.fg` (the SAME tone `RailIconButton` uses for its `active`/`pressed` tiers), not `colors.fgSubtle` (the dimmer tone an ordinary, currently-unselected nav icon uses at rest) — deliberate, since the logo isn't a togglable nav item and should always read as prominent/“selected” by default, exactly as asked. The placeholder box's border color was changed from a hardcoded `colors.fgHover` to `currentColor`, so it (like the default BiDezine SVG mark, already `fill="currentColor"`) automatically tracks whatever color `RailLogoSlot` computes at any given moment with zero extra prop drilling. Documented in the code itself that a future `onClick` prop, if ever added, must be OR'd into the same `isInteractive` check rather than treated as a separate gate — the same “one boolean drives every visual property” discipline this project's own checklist (item 20) already calls out. VERIFIED live via a temporary Playwright script (deleted after use) against the real dev server: with no `logoHref` set (decorative, the current default), the logo's resting color (`oklch(0.985 0 0)`) matches an active rail button's foreground color exactly, and hovering it produces zero change at all (`background`/`color` identical before and after) — confirming the structural gate holds. With a temporary `logoHref` prop wired in for the test only (reverted immediately after), the logo's hover state (`color: oklch(0.922 0 0)`, `background: oklch(0.301 0 0)`) and pressed state (`color: oklch(0.985 0 0)`, `background: oklch(0.348 0 0)`) matched a real rail icon button's own measured hover/pressed computed styles exactly, confirming true parity rather than a visually-similar approximation. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; no `src/ui/*.tsx` primitive was touched (this change is entirely inside the limbo-sandbox `FunctionalRailSidebar.tsx`, so no root package rebuild was required).

rows.title: Badge (neutral / info / dark-surface variants)
rows.detail: Resolved once bidezine's own Badge grew the `success`/`warning`/`info`/`muted` variants, the `weight` (regular/emphasis) axis, and the `tone` (solid/soft) axis in a later pass of this same session — these now map cleanly onto RailNav's neutral/info/atomSurface concepts (muted → neutral, the four status variants → info/positive/caution/negative, tone=soft → the pale/lighter fill RailNav's own atomSurface pattern uses) without needing a bespoke rail-only variant or contaminating Badge's own token authoring with a second design system's literal values (see badge.tsx's own doc comment for the full non-contamination rationale). The user then made an explicit follow-up decision for THIS row specifically: the rail's panel-tree badges (`PanelBadge` in FunctionalRailSidebar.tsx, e.g. “+23”, “New”, “+05”) now default to `variant="muted" weight="regular"` rather than the `variant="secondary"` (bold, `weight="emphasis"` default) they shipped with initially — muted keeps these dense, frequently-repeated inline counts visually receding instead of competing with row content. The user paired this with a general AI-usage guidance rule, now also documented in badge.tsx's own doc comment: an AI composing NEW Badge usage anywhere in the system should default to `weight="regular"`, reserving the bolder `weight="emphasis"` for cases the user explicitly requests or that clearly warrant visual prominence (e.g. an alert-level status, a genuinely prominent count) — emphasis remains a fully valid, supported choice, just not the unexamined default. Verified: PanelBadge in FunctionalRailSidebar.tsx updated to `variant="muted" weight="regular"`; badge.tsx's weight doc comment amended with the AI-usage guidance paragraph, cross-referencing this row.

rows.title: Collapse (motion component)
rows.detail: RESOLVED: rather than reimplementing origin's bespoke Collapse (hand-rolled grid-template-rows: 0fr↔1fr + a setTimeout-based JS timer to force deterministic unmount, driven by its own MOTION.slow/MOTION.ease tokens — see origin's real motion.tsx), the rail's PanelTree group-node CollapsibleContent now animates using bidezine's own already-adopted pattern: `data-[state=open]:animate-collapsible-down data-[state=closed]:animate-collapsible-up overflow-hidden`, the same tw-animate-css keyframe technique our real Accordion primitive already uses for its own auto-height animation — just Collapsible's own dedicated keyframe pair (`--radix-collapsible-content-height`) rather than Accordion's variable. No fixed pixel height anywhere: the height is measured live by Radix from the actual rendered content each open, not hardcoded. This decouples L-7 from H-2–H-6's still-deferred duration/easing TOKEN upgrade — it needed zero new tokens, only reuse of an existing dependency already shipped in package.json. Radix's own CollapsibleContent already unmounts (renders null) once fully closed, satisfying origin's “no lingering DOM/focusable elements” goal via a different, equally valid native mechanism instead of a custom JS timer. IMPLEMENTATION GAP CAUGHT AND FIXED: limbo-factory runs its own separate Tailwind build (via @tailwindcss/vite over its own src/index.css) that never imported tw-animate-css — the root package's src/styles/system.css does import it, but that's pre-compiled into the static dist/system.css this app consumes, so the utility classes would have been dead/no-op CSS in this app specifically. Fixed by adding tw-animate-css as an explicit devDependency in limbo-factory/package.json and importing it in limbo-factory/src/index.css; verified via the live dev server's compiled CSS output that animate-collapsible-down/-up and --radix-collapsible-content-height are real, matched rules, not just class names with nothing behind them. Scoped to FunctionalRailSidebar.tsx's call site only — the shared src/ui/collapsible.tsx primitive itself was not changed, so this doesn't set a system-wide default for every Collapsible usage, only this rail's own PanelTree groups. User approved live (“i see then a[pp]rove you can make it green now”) after trying it in the limbo-factory preview.

Fixed by adding tw-animate-css as an explicit devDependency in limbo-factory/package.json and importing it in limbo-factory/src/index.css; verified via the live dev server's compiled CSS output that animate-collapsible-down/-up and --radix-collapsible-content-height are real, matched rules, not just class names with nothing behind them. Scoped to FunctionalRailSidebar.tsx's call site only — the shared src/ui/collapsible.tsx primitive itself was not changed, so this doesn't set a system-wide default for every Collapsible usage, only this rail's own PanelTree groups. rows.title: PanelTree group-toggle rows looked like a visually different “kind” of element than sibling leaf rows — a deliberate, flagged divergence from bidezine's real Sidebar sub-menu convention
rows.detail: Prompted by “i see the attempt was close but the parent and children look like different elements while the proper behaviour should make them look like same kind of elements but nested in different levels... i could not find a proper primitive that has a nested behavior even in a table or sidebar menus.” Verified visually (screenshot) before any change: group-toggle rows (“System logic”, “Schedules”) rendered at h-8/text-xs/font-medium/text-muted-foreground, while sibling leaf rows (“Rules engine”, “Daily”) rendered at h-9/text-sm/font-normal/full color — visibly two different element families, exactly as reported. CHECKED: bidezine DOES have a real nested-menu primitive family — SidebarMenu/SidebarMenuItem/SidebarMenuButton (top level) plus SidebarMenuSub/SidebarMenuSubItem/SidebarMenuSubButton (one nested level) — confirmed as a faithful port of the vendored reference/shadcn-ui sidebar.tsx and already used for real in site/src/routes/components/SidebarShowcase.tsx (not hypothetical). Two things make it not a clean drop-in here: (1) in that real usage, a group-toggle row and its sibling top-level leaf rows already share the identical SidebarMenuButton recipe — so “same kind of element at a given depth” is already achievable with the real primitive; BUT (2) one level deeper, the established convention deliberately SHRINKS to a smaller, more muted SidebarMenuSubButton (h-7 vs h-8, smaller text) — the opposite of what was asked for, and (3) neither the reference source nor bidezine's own real usage ever nests SidebarMenuSub recursively; every real example is exactly one level deep, while this rail's tree needs three (“System logic” → “Schedules” → “Daily”). Also confirmed SidebarMenuButton calls useSidebar() unconditionally (throws without a real <SidebarProvider> tree — verified in src/ui/sidebar.tsx), so importing it into this panel (a separate, custom composition, not a real Sidebar instance) would require wrapping the whole panel in unrelated Sidebar state machinery just to borrow a className, which doesn't fit. DECIDED: honor the explicit ask over the primitive's own established depth-based convention — gave the group-toggle row the EXACT SAME className/color recipe as the leaf Button (h-9/text-sm/font-normal, resting color var(--foreground)), varying ONLY by depth-based indentation (marginLeft) and the chevron icon (bumped to size-4 to match the leaf icon size too) — the chevron communicates “this expands,” not a different visual tier. This is a deliberate, explicitly flagged departure from bidezine's own real Sidebar sub-menu convention, not a silent one (per the new Sandbox/Limbo fidelity gate in CLAUDE.md). Verified via screenshot in both light and dark app modes: group and leaf rows are now visually indistinguishable except for indentation and the chevron.

rows.title: Rail buttons had zero hover/press feedback despite using the real Button primitive
rows.detail: QA finding, not an origin divergence: prompted by “why is there no hover/press state if Button has those states assigned?” Root cause verified in code and confirmed via getComputedStyle in the browser (background stayed transparent through hover AND press): RailIconButton's className carried `hover:bg-transparent`, which overrode Button's own ghost-variant hover background (`hover:bg-accent`) — presumably because `--accent` is a light-surface token that would look wrong on the dark rail — but nothing was substituted in its place. The correct dark-rail hover/pressed tokens (B-2/B-4, colors.hover/colors.pressed) were already defined on the RailColors type and returned by colorsFor, but were never actually referenced anywhere in the component. The overflow “More” trigger had the exact same gap (no hover feedback, and didn't reflect open state the way origin's OverflowTriggerButton does with darkActiveBg). Fixed: both buttons now track real hover/pressed(/open) state via onMouseEnter/Leave/Down/Up (mirroring origin RailButtonDark's own local-state pattern, since these are dynamic per-instance token values, not static utility classes) and apply colors.hover/colors.pressed/colors.active and colors.fgHover/colors.fgSubtle accordingly; the now-redundant `hover:bg-transparent` overrides were removed. Verified via getComputedStyle: background now genuinely transitions transparent → hover token → pressed token → transparent on mouse enter/down/up/leave.

rows.title: darkBorderStrong's approved value was nearly invisible against the rail surface once actually rendered

rows.title: Raising darkBorderStrong's brightness (M-13) also brightened the rail's own divider lines, since both shared one token
rows.detail: QA finding, not an origin divergence: caught immediately after M-13 shipped — “that helped a lot but it changed the divider line making it too visible, the previous approach was good for the divider line.” Root cause: FunctionalRailSidebar.tsx's two horizontal divider lines (between logo/nav and nav/footer) were reusing colors.border/darkBorderStrong — the SAME token as the browsing-state ring — for an entirely different visual role. That was harmless while darkBorderStrong stayed dim (M-13's whole complaint), but once it was correctly brightened for the ring, the divider brightened right along with it as an unwanted side effect. Confirmed against design-system/src/gallery/RailNav.tsx: origin's own rail has NO divider line at all between these groups — it separates them purely with flex `gap: SPACE[4]`, and darkBorderStrong there is used ONLY for the ring/overflow-menu border, never as a rail-internal divider. Fixed by giving the divider its own dedicated token (darkDividerSubtle, --sidebar-rail-divider) rather than reverting M-13 — the user asked for a proper token, not a rollback: it reuses darkBorderStrong's ORIGINAL, already-reviewed value (oklch(0.256)/oklch(0.254)) verbatim, now correctly scoped to only the role it was always visually right for. RailColors/colorsFor updated with a `divider` field; both divider <div>s switched from colors.border to colors.divider. Verified via getComputedStyle: dividers render back at oklch(0.256)/oklch(0.254) (confirmed unchanged from before M-13) while the ring stays at oklch(0.708 0 0).

rows.title: darkSurface's dark-app-mode value was identical to bidezine's own --background token
rows.detail: QA finding, not an origin divergence: prompted by “when dark mode the rail looks the same color as the background... i dont want it to look like the sidebar color but neither as dark as the background.” Confirmed via getComputedStyle: the rail's real rendered background and the page body's background both resolved to the literal same value, oklch(0.145 0 0) — the rail was indistinguishable from the page in dark app mode, even though B-1/Q2 had already marked this resolved. Constraint discovered while picking a fix: the safe range is narrow and hard-bounded on both sides — a new value must sit ABOVE 0.145 (or it's still not distinct from --background) but BELOW darkHoverBg's already-approved oklch(0.191 0 0) (or the rail's rest state would already look “hovered,” breaking the hover escalation with nowhere left to go). That rules out simply reusing bidezine's own --card/--sidebar dark-theme value (oklch(0.205 0 0), which is what “don't want it to look like the sidebar color” correctly ruled out anyway) — 0.205 sits ABOVE darkHoverBg and would invert rest/hover entirely. Proposed, applied live, and APPROVED by the user (“i like it”): oklch(0.18 0 0) for dark app mode only, a genuinely new number on the same ramp (same precedent as darkHoverBg/darkPressedBg/darkActiveBg/darkActiveHoverBg before it, since no existing bidezine stop falls inside the open (0.145, 0.191) window) — gives the best available separation from --background (delta 0.035) without inverting the hover relationship (delta 0.011 below darkHoverBg) or touching hover/pressed/active's own already-approved values. Light app mode's oklch(0.205 0 0) is untouched (no collision there against a white --background). See the Color token lab tab and B-1.

visual.afterNote: New number, hard-bounded between --background (0.145) and darkHoverBg (0.191).

rows.title: Panel-header “Panel actions” menu had mismatched text alignment across rows
rows.detail: QA finding, not an origin divergence: prompted by “the menubar has a behaviour that when the text has a section for icons the other text options are aligned equally... i see the ellipses dropdown-menu has the text misaligned.” Root cause verified in our own dropdown-menu.tsx (byte-identical to the vendored reference/shadcn-ui menubar.tsx recipe, confirmed by direct comparison): each item TYPE carries its own fixed, unconditional left-padding class, not a padding computed per-menu — plain DropdownMenuItem defaults to `px-2` (8px) unless given the `inset` prop, while DropdownMenuCheckboxItem/RadioItem are hard-coded to `pl-8` (32px) always, to reserve room for their absolutely-positioned checkmark. The Panel actions menu mixed plain DropdownMenuItem rows (“Expand all”, “Collapse all”) with a DropdownMenuCheckboxItem row (“Search box”) with no `inset`, so the two groups landed on different gutters. Measured live via getComputedStyle before the fix: “Expand all”/“Collapse all” at padding-left 8px vs “Search box” at 32px, a real 24px mismatch. Checked against design-system/src/gallery/RailNav.tsx's real PanelMenuRow (the origin source for this exact menu): origin avoids the problem entirely with a different mechanism — every row, checked or not, unconditionally renders a fixed 18×18 left icon slot AND a fixed 18×18 right checkmark slot, so alignment never depends on which item type a given row uses. Since none of our three rows use an icon at all, reproducing origin's icon-slot machinery wasn't warranted here — the minimal, primitive-respecting fix was to add the `inset` prop (a first-class, built-in option on our own DropdownMenuItem, made for exactly this) to “Expand all”/“Collapse all”, forcing them onto the same 32px gutter as “Search box” without fighting CheckboxItem's own built-in checkmark positioning. Verified via getComputedStyle after the fix: all three rows now measure padding-left 32px, and a screenshot confirms all three labels start at the same x-position. The rail's OTHER dropdown (the overflow “More” menu) was checked too and needs no change — every row there is the same plain DropdownMenuItem type with the same icon-plus-label structure, so it was already internally consistent.

rows.title: Search box (real Input primitive) is correct; a separate group-toggle state bug reproduces identically from origin, not introduced by bidezine
rows.detail: Prompted by “the search bar seems buggy, what primitive are we borrowing to build it?” Primitive check: the search field IS our real bidezine Input (src/ui/input.tsx, h-8 pl-7 text-sm) with SearchIcon absolutely positioned in a relative wrapper — same pattern as every other bidezine text field, no hand-rolled input. Live-tested typing, clearing, case sensitivity, and the Panel-actions “Search box” visibility checkbox (which correctly clears the query when disabled) — all correct, no bug found in the Input primitive itself or in filterTree's matching logic. FOUND, but NOT an Input-primitive issue: a group-expand/collapse STATE bug. While searching, matched groups are force-expanded for visibility (effectiveExpanded = expanded ∪ matchIds, a value computed fresh each render), but the chevron's click handler (toggleGroup) only ever reads/writes the underlying `expanded` state, never the merged one. Reproduced live: (1) manually collapse a group (aria-expanded: false), (2) search for one of its children — it auto-expands for the match (aria-expanded: true, correct), (3) click its chevron intending to collapse it — it stays expanded (aria-expanded: true) because the real `expanded` set didn't have that id yet, so the toggle ADDS it instead of removing it, (4) clear the search — the group is now PERMANENTLY stuck expanded, even though the user never actually opened it. Checked against origin's real, currently-shipping source (design-system/src/gallery/RailNav.tsx): origin has the IDENTICAL structural gap — `const expanded = searching ? true : expandedGroups.has(item.id)` with the chevron's onActivate wired to the same unconditional toggleGroup, with no guard for the searching case.
