rows.title: Search box's icon visually overlapped the typed text — wrong primitive composition, not a design decision
rows.detail: QA finding, not an origin divergence: prompted by “the text is overlapping the search icon, i consider that a bug” (a follow-up to M-17's primitive question). Root cause confirmed with getComputedStyle: the search field was a raw Input with a manually-positioned SearchIcon (`absolute left-4`) overlaid via a `relative` wrapper, and the Input's own left padding was overridden with `pl-7` to make room — but the Input primitive's own base recipe already carries `px-3`, and that override never actually won: the rendered padding-left measured 12px (px-3's value), not the intended 28px. Isolated the exact mechanism with tailwind-merge directly (`twMerge('px-3','pl-7')` → `'px-3 pl-7'`, both classes survive — confirmed this is tailwind-merge's documented behavior, not a bug in it, since `pl-7` doesn't fully shadow everything `px-3` provides (the right side), so tailwind-merge correctly leaves both in place and relies on the compiled stylesheet's own rule order to break the tie for the contested property — and in this codebase's Tailwind v4 build, `.px-3`'s declaration happens to win that tie over `.pl-7`, silently discarding the override). This is the well-known “className override didn't take effect” Tailwind pitfall: appending a class later in a className STRING does not guarantee it wins the cascade: only the compiled STYLESHEET's rule order does, and mixing a shorthand (`px-*`) with a same-side longhand (`pl-*`) is exactly the case where that assumption breaks. Fixed at the root by switching to bidezine's own InputGroup/InputGroupAddon/InputGroupInput primitives (src/ui/input-group.tsx) — purpose-built for icon+input composition, already exported from @bidezine/system, and not previously used anywhere in the rail. The icon and input are now real flex siblings with gap-based spacing, so there's no absolute positioning, no padding-override arithmetic, and no cascade-order pitfall at all. Verified via bounding-box measurement with a long test string: icon's right edge and the input's text-start now land at the exact same x-coordinate (869.8px, zero gap/zero overlap) in both light and dark app modes, and by screenshot showing clean, non-overlapping rendering in both the empty (placeholder) and typed states.

rows.title: Rail icon buttons rendered 36px, not the declared 38px, making the right-side gap 2px larger than the left — same root-cause CLASS as M-18, not a new bug type
rows.detail: Prompted by “i notice that the rail has different padding in the left and right, the right padding looks larger... whats the recommended pattern for our system so the rail can hug the content and respect top/bottom/right/left padding?” Measured live: the rail container's own padding is correctly uniform (`p-2`, 8px computed on all sides — confirmed via getComputedStyle, not the bug). The asymmetry was downstream of that: RailIconButton (and the overflow-menu trigger, and the disabled Profile button) all use Button's `size="icon"` variant (which carries the shorthand `size-9`, 36px) PLUS an explicit `h-[38px] w-[38px]` className meant to override it to the rail's actual 38px spec. That override never won: measured bounding box was 36×36, not 38×38 — confirmed via `twMerge('size-9','h-[38px] w-[38px]')` → both classes survive (same category as M-18: `size-*` and `h-*`/`w-*` aren't in tailwind-merge's same conflict group, so neither gets dropped, and the compiled stylesheet lets `size-9` win the cascade tie). Because the button's rendered box was 2px SMALLER than the 38px content area in a flex-col rail with no cross-axis stretch on a definite-size child, the shortfall wasn’t split evenly — the button anchored to the LEFT/start edge (default cross-axis alignment for a sized flex item) and the missing 2px accumulated entirely on the right, producing exactly the visible asymmetry reported (left gap 8px, right gap 10px, confirmed via getBoundingClientRect on the rendered DOM before the fix). RECOMMENDED PATTERN (the direct answer to “what's the recommended form”): when overriding one of Button's built-in `size` variants (`icon`/`icon-xs`/`icon-sm`/`icon-lg`, all shorthand `size-*` utilities) to a custom one-off dimension, override with the matching `size-[<value>]` shorthand, never split `h-*`/`w-*` longhand classes — confirmed via twMerge directly that `size-[38px]` correctly replaces `size-9` (`twMerge('size-9','size-[38px]')` → `'size-[38px]'`), whereas `h-[38px] w-[38px]` does not. Applied this fix to all 3 affected Button call sites (RailIconButton, the overflow “More” trigger, the disabled Profile button); the plain, non-Button logo slot `<div>` was checked too and was ALREADY correct (no competing shorthand class to conflict with). Verified via getBoundingClientRect after the fix: all rail buttons now measure exactly 38×38 with an equal 8px gap on both the left and right against the rail's own padding, confirmed by screenshot.

rows.title: Real `adjacentContent` (added in M-7) silently disappeared entirely whenever the browsing panel was closed, instead of persisting and reclaiming the freed width
rows.detail: Prompted directly by the user: “when i collapse the sidebar the block disapears i want to know what happened with it when there is no sidebar.” Root cause: `<Presence present={Boolean(openSection)}>` wrapped the ENTIRE `ResizablePanelGroup` — both the browsing panel AND the `adjacentContent` panel — as its single child, gated by an outer `{displaySection && (...)}`. `displaySection` itself almost never actually goes falsy (a `lastOpenSectionRef` retains the last-open section forever, and `openPanel`'s initial state is truthy), so it was NOT the guard causing the disappearance; `Presence`'s own mount/unmount behavior was. Once the browsing panel's own close animation finished playing, `Presence` unmounted its whole child — the whole group, including `adjacentContent`, which conceptually represents the rest of a real consumer's page and should never vanish just because a flyout panel closed. FIXED by moving `<Presence>` INWARD to wrap only the browsing panel's own animated content div (the bordered/elevated/shadow-md surface with the fade/zoom in/out classes) instead of the whole group — `ResizablePanelGroup` and both `ResizablePanel`s now render unconditionally, so `adjacentContent` (or its default placeholder) always stays mounted. The browsing panel itself now visually shrinks to 0 width via `react-resizable-panels`' own real `collapsible`/`collapsedSize={0}` props plus an imperative `panelRef` (typed via a locally-declared `RailPanelHandle` interface mirroring the library's real `PanelImperativeHandle` — the package isn't a direct `limbo-factory` dependency, only transitive via `@bidezine/system`, so it can't be `import type`'d directly) — reusing the primitive's own real collapse mechanism rather than hand-rolling a width animation. Sequencing detail (the part that needed the most care): calling `.collapse()` synchronously the instant `openSection` goes falsy would snap the panel to 0 width immediately and clip the existing fade/zoom-out exit animation (L-15/L-16) before it ever gets to play — so `.collapse()` is instead called from the animated div's own `onAnimationEnd` handler (guarded with `event.target !== event.currentTarget` to ignore any bubbled child animations), firing only once the CSS exit animation has genuinely finished; expanding (`.expand()`) happens immediately in a `useEffect` keyed on `openSection`, since there's no reverse animation-completion concern for opening — the panel needs real width available before the fade/zoom-in animation can be visible at all. A new `onResize` handler on the browsing panel keeps `openPanel` React state in sync if a user manually drags the handle past the panel's own `minSize` (which enabling `collapsible` allows the library to auto-snap-collapse on) or drags a collapsed panel back open — without this, a manual drag-collapse would leave `openPanel` pointing at a section whose panel is actually visually collapsed, desyncing the rail icon's own active/browsing highlight until the next click. Verified: `limbo-factory` `npx tsc --noEmit` clean and `npm run build` (production `vite build`) succeeds cleanly after the change. CORRECTION (see M-21): this fix's own mechanism (Presence-inward + collapsible/collapsedSize) was structurally correct, but a separate, pre-existing layout bug (the composite's outer width chain never actually reaching the stage's full available width) made the fix's real effects nearly invisible — M-20's own `npm run build` verification never caught this because no live browser measurement was done at the time.

rows.title: Two follow-on bugs surfaced once M-20 was tried live: (1) `adjacentContent` rendered but nearly invisible (tiny, ~41px sliver) with unexplained blank space beyond it; (2) the resize handle stayed visible, floating with nothing on its left, once the browsing panel was fully collapsed
rows.detail: Prompted directly by the user with a screenshot: “I see two issues number one when I collapse the sidebar, the resize element still visible... and I don't see the widget that is supposed to be at the right side that feels the area... This is important to me so then we can create contract and verify behaviors.” Investigated with a scratch Playwright script (`chromium.launch()` against the live `limbo-factory` dev server) doing real `getBoundingClientRect`/`data-panel` measurements — not a screenshot glance — per this project's own Primitive Fidelity Checklist (verify by render, not by number; measure, don't eyeball). Root cause of bug (1), traced by walking the DOM ancestor chain from a `[data-panel]` node outward to the app shell: `FunctionalRailSidebar`'s own outer row (`<div className="flex">`, no width) AND its two mount-site wrappers in `FullRailPreview.tsx` (`<div className="dark:hidden">`/`<div className="hidden dark:block">`, also no width) sat inside `App.tsx`'s `FillHeight`/`QuadrantLayout` chain, which correctly provides `w-full` all the way down — but a `w-full` ancestor chain is worthless if ANY link in it is a plain shrink-to-content block with no width class of its own; live measurement confirmed the whole composite rendered at only ~443–460px while its actual available stage was ~508px (and would be far larger in a real, non-half-quadrant consuming app). Confirmed via the SAME live measurement that `ResizablePanelGroup`'s `flex-1` was working exactly as designed — it had no real space to grow into, because its own flex-ROW parent was self-sizing to content instead of filling the stage. FIXED by adding `w-full` to `FunctionalRailSidebar`'s own outer row (`limbo-factory/src/components/FunctionalRailSidebar.tsx`) AND to both wrapper divs in `RailNavStatusPreview` (`limbo-factory/src/components/FullRailPreview.tsx`) — verified live: the group's measured width grew from 381px to 398px in this sandbox's own constrained stage, and `adjacentContent`'s own rendered width grew from 41px to 133px (now clearly visible, confirmed by screenshot), with zero unaccounted blank space beyond the composite's right edge. This is a preview-harness-only fix — `FunctionalRailSidebar` itself already correctly used `flex-1` internally; a real production consumer's own page shell, not a sandbox preview wrapper, determines the composite's real available width, so this bug was specific to `limbo-factory`'s own mount site, not a defect a real consumer would necessarily hit (though the underlying lesson — every ancestor in a `w-full` chain must itself declare `w-full`/an equivalent stretch, or the chain silently breaks at that link — is a general contract worth restating for any future consumer wiring this component up). Root cause of bug (2): `ResizableHandle` rendered unconditionally regardless of the browsing panel's own collapsed state, so once M-20's collapse mechanism actually became visible (after fixing bug 1), the handle was left floating with nothing meaningful on its left. FIXED by adding real component state, `isBrowsingPanelCollapsed` (not derived from `openPanel`, which flips the instant a rail icon is clicked, before the exit animation has even started — using it directly would make the handle vanish while the panel was still visibly animating closed), updated from the SAME `onResize` callback M-20 already wired to the browsing `ResizablePanel` (`size.inPixels <= 0`), and conditionally rendering `{!isBrowsingPanelCollapsed && <ResizableHandle withHandle />}`. This ties the handle's disappearance to the exact moment the panel has actually finished collapsing (post-animation, via `.collapse()`’s own real resize event) — the same moment `adjacentContent` visibly reclaims the freed space — rather than an earlier, premature moment that would look broken mid-animation. VERIFIED CONTRACT (live, via the same Playwright measurement harness, covering the full round-trip the user asked to see “verified”): panel open → browsing panel ~264px, adjacentContent ~133px, handle visible (1 real separator + 1 zero-sized hidden-theme duplicate); collapse click → browsing panel exactly 0px, adjacentContent grows to fill the ENTIRE freed width (~398px, matching the group's full measured width), handle fully removed from layout (0 real separators, only the zero-sized hidden-theme duplicate remains); re-open via the same rail icon → browsing panel and adjacentContent both return to their exact original widths (264px/133px) and the handle reappears — confirmed by screenshot at every step, not by property inspection alone. `limbo-factory` `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run build` (production `vite build`) both verified clean after both fixes.

rows.title: Collapsed-state rail-to-widget gap measured 24px, not the intended 8px `RAIL_PANEL_GAP` — not the resize handle (already confirmed removed by M-21), but the placeholder's own left padding stacking on top of the real outer gap
rows.detail: Prompted directly by the user: “when collpased it seems like there is a larger gap mostly becasue the resizible area still there but invisible, we should completaly remove it so there is a proper gap between the rail and the widget.” First checked the user's own hypothesis with a fresh live Playwright measurement (not assumed correct or incorrect from memory): confirmed the browsing `ResizablePanel` genuinely collapses to a real, measured 0px width, and `ResizableHandle` is fully absent from the DOM (`page.$$('[role="separator"]')` returned zero elements) — M-21's conditional-render fix holds; there is no leftover invisible resizable element occupying space. The REAL gap: rail's right edge measured at x=886, the `adjacentContent` `ResizablePanel`'s own left edge at x=894 (a correct 8px, matching `RAIL_PANEL_GAP`) — but the visible grey `Skeleton` block inside `AdjacentContentPlaceholder` only started at x=910, an additional 16px in from the panel's own edge, because `AdjacentContentPlaceholder` unconditionally applies `p-4` (16px on all four sides) so real `adjacentContent` has breathing room from the browsing panel's own right edge while it's open. rows.title: Direct @radix-ui/react-dropdown-menu import
rows.detail: Decided: no separate dark-surface DropdownMenu wrapper needed. The Rail's own overflow (“More”) menu now locally redefines the shared DropdownMenuContent/DropdownMenuItem primitive's own CSS vars (--popover/--popover-foreground/--accent/--accent-foreground/--border) via an inline style at that one call site, sourced from the same colors object already driving the Rail's trigger button — every other DropdownMenu in the app is untouched. Confirmed as final. Follow-up (this pass): the overflow menu's icon+label color now tracks the SAME three tokens RailIconButton's own icon uses at rest/hover/persistent-selected (`colors.fgSubtle`/`colors.fgHover`/`colors.fg`, via new `--dm-icon-fg-rest`/`--dm-icon-fg-hover`/`--dm-icon-fg-selected` vars), and the row background's hover/pressed/selected states reuse `colors.hover`/`colors.pressed`/`colors.active` via the `--accent`/`--accent-pressed`/`--accent-selected` vars already set here — confirming this row's own “fill” (background) states already fully associate with the Rail's own fill tokens, live-verified via Playwright (identical computed colors at rest/hover/selected on both sides). CORRECTION (see M-4): a first stashed row was briefly converted into a real DropdownMenuSub, then reverted — see M-4 for what replaced it. Separately, a genuine bug surfaced and was fixed: the popup's `--border` var was being fed `colors.hairline`, which in “bidezine” (adjusted) mode is itself the literal passthrough string `"var(--border)"` — redeclaring `--border: var(--border)` is a self-reference, invalid at computed-value time, and was silently resolving to the popover's own near-white `currentColor` instead (reported as “the white line might be too strong”). Fixed with a small `nonCircularVar()` guard (FunctionalRailSidebar.tsx) that omits the local override whenever it would just be a self-reference, letting the element fall through to the real, correctly-scoped ambient `--border` token — live-verified: dark theme now resolves to `oklch(1 0 0 / 0.1)` (the design system's own subtle dark hairline) instead of the broken `oklch(0.985 0 0)` (near-white) fallback. CORRECTION (see L-49): this row's own “fill states already fully associate” claim above only ever covered the Rail's default and active tiers — the middle “browsing” tier (panel open, nothing selected yet) had no overflow-menu equivalent at all until L-49 added `DropdownMenuItem`'s `isOpen` prop.

rows.title: Custom hand-rolled tooltip (portal + fixed positioning)
rows.detail: Approved by the user (“I like it, make it green”). Our Tooltip (Radix-based, portal built-in) is an effectively clean replacement. Caveat found during Build (see L-1/L-2): our Tooltip shows on hover unconditionally by default — the origin's per-instance suppression rules (LogoSlotDark always shows; RailButtonDark suppresses when active/browsing/disabled) are NOT automatic and must be wired per call site. Do this by conditionally omitting the Tooltip wrapper for the suppressed state, never by toggling Radix Tooltip's own `open` prop between `false` and `undefined` — that flips the component between controlled/uncontrolled and triggers a React runtime warning (confirmed via manual testing in the limbo-factory preview).

rows.title: ResizeObserver overflow budget
rows.detail: Built as an explicit CONTRACT, not an implicit recalculation: new src/hooks/useOverflowFit.ts — measures rows via an author-provided rowSelector (not a generic tag selector), enforces a hard maxVisible ceiling (RAIL_MAX_VISIBLE_SECTIONS = 12, raised from the initial 7 per explicit user follow-up once real section counts made 7 too restrictive), floors the result at 1, and recalculates via ResizeObserver. Wired into FunctionalRailSidebar.tsx in place of the old inline useEffect/querySelector("button") block; RailIconButton's own Button now carries data-rail-row="" as the explicit measurement marker. Truncation half of the contract: RailIconButton is icon-only (label is sr-only) so there is no rail-track text to truncate; overflow-menu item labels and panel-tree labels already truncate (established in earlier session work). Scrolling half of the contract: the rail track itself is deliberately NEVER scrollable by design (items that don't fit are stashed into the “More” overflow menu, not scrolled past) — and the overflow menu's own scrolling need is already satisfied for free by DropdownMenuContent (src/ui/dropdown-menu.tsx), which composes a real ScrollArea internally capped at Radix's own measured --radix-dropdown-menu-content-available-height. No new scrolling code was needed. Verified: limbo-factory npx tsc --noEmit clean.

rows.title: Panel resize handle (mouse-drag)
rows.detail: Resolved via bidezine's own real Resizable primitive (react-resizable-panels, ResizablePanelGroup/ResizablePanel/ResizableHandle — src/ui/resizable.tsx), not a hand-rolled mousedown/mousemove reimplementation. CORRECTED finding vs. the original L-35/L-36/L-37 implementation: this project's installed react-resizable-panels (v4.12.2) re-measures the group's own rendered size LIVE and re-derives each panel's pixel-based percentage on every resize (confirmed by tracing groupSize through the library's own compiled resize/layout functions), not just once at mount as the original doc-comment assumed — so the fixed PANEL_GROUP_WIDTH pixel-width workaround was unnecessary and has been removed; ResizablePanelGroup now sizes itself naturally via flex-1 inside its real flex-row parent, exactly like a real consuming app's shell would provide. The invisible/aria-hidden/pointer-events-none filler panel (a bookkeeping-only stand-in for real page content this sandbox never had) is replaced with a REAL, visible adjacentContent panel — FunctionalRailSidebar now accepts an optional adjacentContent?: React.ReactNode prop, rendered in a second ResizablePanel (min width ADJACENT_CONTENT_MIN_WIDTH, renamed from PANEL_FILLER_MIN_WIDTH), falling back to a lightweight “Page content” placeholder when a consumer doesn't supply one — so the resize drag genuinely reflows something, not an inert void; all three existing consumers (App.tsx, CompareVisuals.tsx, FullRailPreview.tsx) continue to compile and render using that default placeholder. Gap workaround reversed, per explicit user request: the outer rail-to-panel gap is restored to a real, honest RAIL_PANEL_GAP = 8 flex gap (matching the approved panelGap, F-4/L-44) instead of relying on PANEL_SHADOW_INSET's own padding to double as the visual gap (that reliance was flagged by the user as an undocumented workaround, unused anywhere else in this design system). Because ResizablePanelGroup's own un-removable internal overflow: hidden still needs SOME inset before the panel's shadow-md to avoid clipping, and doubling both the new outer gap AND the old full inset would reproduce the L-38 double-gap bug (16px instead of 8px), the panel's LEFT-side shadow inset is set to 0 (top/right/bottom keep the full PANEL_SHADOW_INSET, so the L-37 right-side corner-bleed fix is untouched) — a deliberate, explicitly documented tradeoff: the top-left/bottom-left corner shadow-bleed is clipped flush on that one side only, accepted because the left edge faces the dark rail (least visually prominent side for a soft corner shadow) and 8px of real, honest gap space already exists there regardless of the shadow's own bleed radius. Verified: limbo-factory npx tsc --noEmit clean; live dev server (127.0.0.1:4199) confirmed responsive after the change.

rows.title: logoLabel default = “BiDezine”
rows.detail:
Expanded well beyond the original one-line finding into a full LOGO CONTRACT, per explicit user request. Mandatory process: before wiring any specific logo into a real consumer's Rail Sidebar, the AI/implementer MUST explicitly ask the requester for their logo, in SVG format, sized to this slot's real rendered box (38×38px rail-button hit area; the mark itself renders at 24×24px / `size-6`, matching this component's own default `BIDEZINE_LOGO_VIEWBOX` 26.064×24 aspect as a sizing reference) — never invent, guess, or auto-generate a logo (this generalizes the standing Q3 rule, previously scoped to the Intake/factory-line “Logo-import slot” UI element, to this component's own real, shipped prop surface). If the requester has no logo ready, exactly two explicit interim states are acceptable, never silently substituted for each other: (1) leave `logoIcon` unset — renders this design system's own default BiDezine mark as a clearly-temporary stand-in (the pre-existing default behavior), or (2) set the new `logoPlaceholder` prop to `true` — renders an empty, dashed-border box with no mark at all, for consumers who don't want BiDezine's own branding shown even temporarily. `FunctionalRailSidebar` (limbo-factory/src/components/FunctionalRailSidebar.tsx) gained three new props to support this: `logoLabel?: string` (already existed conceptually as a hardcoded “BiDezine” string in the tooltip; now a real, documented prop, still defaulting to “BiDezine”), `logoIcon?: React.ReactNode` (a real inline ``, per CLAUDE.md's inline-SVG rule), and `logoPlaceholder?: boolean` (the empty-box interim state). Additionally, per explicit user request: `logoHref?: string` — when provided, the logo slot itself becomes a real hyperlink (``) that navigates on click; when omitted, the slot stays a plain non-interactive `
` (the pre-existing behavior, unchanged for consumers that don't want a clickable logo). The hover tooltip (Radix `Tooltip`, always shown regardless of rail state, per M-5/L-1) now reads from `logoLabel` instead of a hardcoded string, so a consumer supplying their own `logoIcon`/`logoHref` also gets their own brand name surfaced in the tooltip, never a leftover “BiDezine” string. Verified: limbo-factory npx tsc --noEmit clean.

Additionally, per explicit user request: `logoHref?: string` — when provided, the logo slot itself becomes a real hyperlink (``) that navigates on click; when omitted, the slot stays a plain non-interactive `
` (the pre-existing behavior, unchanged for consumers that don't want a clickable logo). The hover tooltip (Radix `Tooltip`, always shown regardless of rail state, per M-5/L-1) now reads from `logoLabel` instead of a hardcoded string, so a consumer supplying their own `logoIcon`/`logoHref` also gets their own brand name surfaced in the tooltip, never a leftover “BiDezine” string. Verified: limbo-factory npx tsc --noEmit clean.

rows.title: Sandbox fidelity gate — className-override-vs-primitive-shorthand bugs found twice in one session (M-18, M-19)
rows.detail: Two separate rendering bugs (search icon overlapping text, rail buttons rendering 2px undersized) traced to the identical root cause: a className meant to override a bidezine primitive's own built-in shorthand utility class (Input's px-3, Button's size-9) silently lost the compiled Tailwind stylesheet's cascade tie, even though the override looked correct in source and appeared later in the className string. Because the same failure class repeated on two different primitives in one session, the lesson was generalized directly into CLAUDE.md's new “Sandbox/Limbo fidelity” section (covering className-override verification, suppressed-state replacement wiring, hand-rolled markup, isolated-swatch re-verification, doc-vs-code drift, faithfully-reproduced origin bugs, and short-demo-content overflow testing) rather than left as a one-off fix, so future Limbo occupants inherit the check automatically. See LIMBO-PROTOCOL-LOG.md's flaws log for the full rationale.
